title.zh: 卷四百二十九 列傳第一百八十八 道學三 朱熹 張栻
title.en: Volume 429 Biographies 188: Taoist Scholars 3: Zhu Xi, Zhang Shi
title.raw: 卷四百二十九 列傳第一百八十八 道學三 朱熹 張栻 Volume 429 Biographies 188: Taoist Scholars 3: Zhu Xi, Zhang Shi

sentences.zh: 朱熹 張栻

translations.literal: Zhu Xi; Zhang Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi.

sentences.zh: 朱熹，字元晦，一字仲晦，徽州婺源人。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi, styled Yuanhui, with another style Zhonghui, was a man of Wuyuan in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi, whose style was Yuanhui and who also used the style Zhonghui, came from Wuyuan in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 父松字喬年，中進士第。

translations.literal: His father Song, styled Qiaonian, attained the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhu Song, styled Qiaonian, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 胡世將、謝克家薦之，除秘書省正字。

translations.literal: Hu Shijiang and Xie Kejia recommended him, and he was appointed Rectifier in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Hu Shijiang and Xie Kejia, he was appointed Secretariat Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎都督川陝、荊、襄軍馬，招松為屬，辭。

translations.literal: Zhao Ding, as overall commander of the armies of Sichuan, Shaanxi, Jing, and Xiang, invited Song to serve on his staff; Song declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ding was made overall commander of the forces in Sichuan, Shaanxi, Jing, and Xiang, he asked Song to join his staff, but Song refused.

sentences.zh: 鼎再相，除校書郎，遷著作郎。

translations.literal: When Ding again became chief councilor, Song was appointed Collator and then promoted to Compiler in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao Ding returned to the chief ministership, Song was made a Collator and later promoted to Compiler in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 以御史中丞常同薦，除度支員外郎，兼史館校勘，歷司勳、吏部郎。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of the Censor-in-Chief Chang Tong, he was appointed Vice Director in the Revenue Bureau, concurrently Reviser in the Historiography Institute, and served successively as Director in the Bureau of Honors and as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Censor-in-Chief Chang Tong, he was appointed Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau and concurrent Historiography Institute Reviser, and later served as Director in the Bureau of Honors and in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 秦檜決策議和，松與同列上章，極言其不可。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui decided to pursue peace negotiations, Song and his colleagues submitted memorials vehemently declaring that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui resolved to negotiate peace with the Jurchens, Song and his colleagues memorialized the throne in the strongest terms that such a course was unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 檜怒，風御史論松懷異自賢，出知饒州，未上，卒。

translations.literal: Hui was enraged and prompted the censors to accuse Song of harboring dissent and making a show of his own worth; Song was sent out as prefect of Raozhou, but before he took up the post he died.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui, furious, had the censors denounce Song for disloyal opinions and self-righteousness; Song was appointed prefect of Raozhou but died before he could assume office.

sentences.zh: 熹幼穎悟，甫能言，父指天示之曰：「天也。」

translations.literal: Xi was clever from childhood; as soon as he could speak, his father pointed to the sky and showed him, saying, "This is Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Xi was exceptionally bright; barely able to speak, he was shown the sky by his father, who said, "That is Heaven."

sentences.zh: 熹問曰：「天之上何物？」

translations.literal: Xi asked, "What is above Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Xi asked, "What lies above Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 松異之。

translations.literal: Song marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: His father was astonished.

sentences.zh: 就傅，授以《孝經》，一閱，題其上曰：「不若是，非人也。」

translations.literal: When he went to his teacher and was given the Classic of Filial Piety, after one reading he inscribed on it, "If one is not like this, one is not human."
translations.idiomatic: Once he began formal study and was taught the Classic of Filial Piety, he read it through once and wrote on the book, "Anyone who does not live this way is not truly human."

sentences.zh: 嘗從群兒戲沙上，獨端坐以指畫沙，視之，八卦也。

translations.literal: Once, while playing in the sand with other children, he alone sat upright and traced figures in the sand with his finger; on looking, they were the Eight Trigrams.
translations.idiomatic: Once, playing in the sand with other boys, he sat apart and traced figures with his finger; they formed the Eight Trigrams of the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 年十八貢於鄉，中紹興十八年進士第。

translations.literal: At eighteen he presented himself as a candidate in the prefectural examination and in the eighteenth year of Shaoxing attained the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he qualified in the prefectural examination, and in 1148 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 主泉州同安簿，選邑秀民充弟子員，日與講說聖賢修己治人之道，禁女婦之為僧道者。

translations.literal: He served as registrar of Tong'an in Quanzhou, selected outstanding local youths as academy students, and daily lectured on the ways of the sages for self-cultivation and ordering others, forbidding women to become Buddhist or Daoist clergy.
translations.idiomatic: As registrar of Tong'an in Quanzhou, he chose promising local youths as students and lectured daily on how the sages cultivated themselves and governed others, while forbidding women to take monastic vows.

sentences.zh: 罷歸請祠，監潭州南嶽廟。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned home and requested a sinecure post, and was made custodian of the Southern Marchmount Temple in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he returned home, sought a nominal temple appointment, and was made custodian of the Southern Marchmount Temple in Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，以輔臣薦，與徐度、呂廣問、韓元吉同召，以疾辭。

translations.literal: The next year, on the recommendation of chief ministers, he was summoned together with Xu Du, Lü Guangwen, and Han Yuangji, but declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on the recommendation of senior ministers, he was summoned to court along with Xu Du, Lü Guangwen, and Han Yuangji, but declined citing illness.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，詔求直言，熹上封事言：「聖躬雖未有過失，而帝王之學不可以不熟講。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, an edict called for forthright counsel; Xi submitted a sealed memorial saying, "Though Your Majesty's person has as yet no faults, the learning of an emperor cannot go without thorough study.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne and called for frank counsel, Xi submitted a sealed memorial: "Though Your Majesty has as yet committed no personal fault, the learning proper to a ruler cannot be left unstudied.

sentences.zh: 朝政雖未有闕遺，而修攘之計不可以不早定。

translations.literal: Though court administration has as yet no omissions, plans for internal cultivation and external defense cannot go undecided early.
translations.idiomatic: Though the court's governance has shown no glaring lapse, plans for strengthening the state within and resisting enemies without must be settled without delay.

sentences.zh: 利害休戚雖不可遍舉，而本原之地不可以不加意。

translations.literal: Though profit and harm, weal and woe cannot all be enumerated, the root source cannot go without attention.
translations.idiomatic: Though one cannot list every matter of profit and loss or public and private welfare, the root of government must not be neglected.

sentences.zh: 陛下毓德之初，親御簡策，不過風誦文辭，吟詠情性，又頗留意於老子、釋氏之書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Your Majesty's nurturing of virtue, in personally handling the bamboo slips, it has been no more than reciting literary compositions and chanting to express feeling, and Your Majesty has also paid considerable attention to the books of Laozi and the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: In the years when Your Majesty was cultivating virtue, study has meant chiefly reciting belles-lettres and composing poetry, with considerable attention also given to Laozi and Buddhist writings.

sentences.zh: 夫記誦詞藻，非所以探淵源而出治道；

translations.literal: For memorization and literary ornament are not the means to probe the deep source and bring forth the way of governance;
translations.idiomatic: Memorization and literary polish are not how one probes the deep springs of order and brings forth the way of governance;

sentences.zh: 虛無寂滅，非所以貫本末而立大中。

translations.literal: emptiness, nothingness, and extinction are not the means to thread root and branch and establish the great Mean.
translations.idiomatic: nor are emptiness, quiescence, and annihilation the means to join root and branch and establish the great Mean.

sentences.zh: 帝王之學，必先格物致知，以極夫事物之變，使義理所存，纖悉畢照，則自然意誠心正，而可以應天下之務。」

translations.literal: The learning of an emperor must first investigate things and extend knowledge to the utmost, reaching the full range of change in affairs so that where principle resides is minutely illuminated; then intent becomes sincere and the mind upright, and one can respond to the tasks of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The learning of a ruler must begin with investigating things and extending knowledge to the utmost, comprehending every change in affairs until moral principle is illuminated in every detail; then sincerity of intent and rectitude of mind follow naturally, and one can meet the demands of governing the realm."

sentences.zh: 次言：「修攘之計不時定者，講和之說誤之也。

translations.literal: He next said, "That plans for cultivation and defense are not settled in time is because talk of negotiated peace has misled us.
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "The reason plans for internal strength and external defense are never settled in time is that the doctrine of negotiated peace has led us astray.

sentences.zh: 夫金人於我有不共戴天之仇，則不可和也明矣。

translations.literal: The Jurchens bear with us a hatred that cannot be worn on the same cap—clearly peace is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens are our mortal enemies; that peace with them is impossible should be obvious.

sentences.zh: 願斷以義理之公，閉關絕約，任賢使能，立紀綱，厲風俗。

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty decide by the public standard of principle, close the passes and sever treaties, appoint the worthy and employ the able, establish institutions, and invigorate custom.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decide by the impartial standard of moral principle: close the borders, break off treaties, appoint worthy men and employ the capable, establish institutions, and revive public morals.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，國富兵強，視吾力之強弱，觀彼釁之淺深，徐起而圖之。」

translations.literal: After several years, when the state is rich and the army strong, observing the strength or weakness of our power and the shallowness or depth of their provocations, rise gradually and plan against them."
translations.idiomatic: After several years, when the state is wealthy and the army strong, judge by our own strength and by the gravity of their provocations, then move deliberately to strike."

sentences.zh: 次言：「四海利病，係欺民之休戚，斯民休戚，係守令之賢否。

translations.literal: He next said, "The profit and harm of the four seas are tied to the people's weal and woe; the people's weal and woe are tied to whether prefects and magistrates are worthy or not.
translations.idiomatic: He next observed: "The welfare of the whole realm depends on the people's fortune; the people's fortune depends on whether local prefects and magistrates are capable or corrupt.

sentences.zh: 監司者守令之綱，朝廷者監司之本也。

translations.literal: Intendant-commissioners are the net over prefects and magistrates; the court is the root of the intendant-commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Intendant-commissioners hold prefects and magistrates in check; the court holds intendant-commissioners in check.

sentences.zh: 欲斯民之得其所，本原之地亦在朝廷而已。

translations.literal: If one wishes the people to find their proper place, the root source too lies only in the court.
translations.idiomatic: If the people are to prosper, the root of reform lies in the court itself.

sentences.zh: 今之監司，姦贓狼籍、肆虐以病民者，莫非宰執、臺諫之親舊賓客。

translations.literal: Among today's intendant-commissioners, those whose corruption is notorious and who tyrannize the people are none other than the kin, old friends, and clients of chief ministers and censorial remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: Today's corrupt intendant-commissioners who prey on the people are almost all relatives, old friends, or clients of chief ministers and censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 其已失勢者，既按見其交私之狀而斥去之；

translations.literal: Those who have already lost power have had their private dealings exposed and been dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Those who have already fallen from power have been exposed for their private dealings and dismissed;

sentences.zh: 尚在勢者，豈無其人，顧陛下無自而知之耳。」

translations.literal: among those still in power, are there not such men? Only Your Majesty has no means to know them for himself."
translations.idiomatic: but among those still in favor, are there not such men as well? Your Majesty simply has no way to learn of them on his own."

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，復召。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing he was summoned again.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Longxing era he was summoned again.

sentences.zh: 入對，其一言：「大學之道在乎格物以致其知。

translations.literal: In audience, his first statement: "The way of the Great Learning lies in investigating things to extend knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: In audience, his first statement was: "The way of the Great Learning lies in investigating things to extend knowledge.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖有生知之性，高世之行，而未嘗隨事以觀理，即理以應事。

translations.literal: Your Majesty though possesses the nature of innate knowledge and conduct that transcends the age, yet has never observed principle through affairs or responded to affairs by principle.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, though possessed of innate knowledge and conduct that transcends the age, has never observed principle through affairs or responded to affairs by principle.

sentences.zh: 是以舉措之間動涉疑貳，聽納之際未免蔽欺，平治之效所以未著。」

translations.literal: Therefore in action you repeatedly fall into doubt and hesitation, and in listening and accepting you cannot avoid deception and occlusion—so the effect of tranquil governance has not yet appeared."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in action you repeatedly fall into doubt and hesitation, and in listening and accepting you cannot avoid deception and occlusion—so the effect of tranquil governance has not yet appeared."

sentences.zh: 其二言：「君父之讐不與共戴天。

translations.literal: His second statement: "The enemy of one's lord and father is not one with whom one can live under the same sky.
translations.idiomatic: His second statement was: "The enemy of one's lord and father is not one with whom one can live under the same sky.

sentences.zh: 今日所當為者，非戰無以復讐，非守無以制勝。」

translations.literal: What must be done today is this: without fighting there is no means to avenge the wrong, and without defending there is no means to prevail."
translations.idiomatic: What must be done today is this: without fighting there is no means to avenge the wrong, and without defending there is no means to prevail."

sentences.zh: 且陳古先聖王所以強本折衝、威制遠人之道。

translations.literal: He also expounded the ways by which the ancient sage-kings strengthened the root, repelled enemies at the frontier, and overawed distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: He also expounded the ways by which the ancient sage-kings strengthened the root, repelled enemies at the frontier, and overawed distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 時相湯思退方倡和議，除熹武學博士，待次。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Councillor Tang Situi was advocating peace talks; Xi was appointed Doctor of the Military Academy, to await his turn.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chief Councillor Tang Situi was advocating peace talks; Zhu Xi was appointed Doctor of the Military Academy, to await his turn.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，促就職，既至而洪适為相，復主和，論不合，歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao he was urged to take office; when he arrived Hong Shi was chief councillor and again favored peace—their views did not accord, and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qiandao era he was urged to take office; when he arrived Hong Shi was chief councillor and again favored peace. Their views did not accord, and he returned home.

sentences.zh: 三年，陳俊卿、劉珙薦為樞密院編修官，待次。

translations.literal: In the third year Chen Junqing and Liu Gong recommended him as compiler at the Privy Council, to await his turn.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Chen Junqing and Liu Gong recommended him as compiler at the Privy Council, to await his turn.

sentences.zh: 五年，丁內艱。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he mourned his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he mourned his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 六年，工部侍郎胡銓以詩人薦，與王庭珪同召，以未終喪辭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Vice Minister of Works Hu Quan recommended him as a poet; he was summoned together with Wang Tinggui, but declined because mourning was not yet completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Vice Minister of Works Hu Quan recommended him as a poet; he was summoned together with Wang Tinggui, but declined because mourning was not yet completed.

sentences.zh: 七年，既免喪，復召，以祿不及養辭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when mourning was completed, he was summoned again but declined on the ground that his salary had not sufficed to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when mourning was completed, he was summoned again but declined on the ground that his salary had not sufficed to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 九年，梁克家相，申前命，又辭。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Liang Kejia became chief councillor, the previous appointment was reiterated, and he declined again.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when Liang Kejia became chief councillor, the previous appointment was reiterated, and he declined again.

sentences.zh: 克家奏熹屢召不起，宜蒙褒錄，執政俱稱之，上曰：「熹安貧守道，廉退可嘉。」

translations.literal: Kejia memorialized that Xi had repeatedly been summoned without rising—he ought to receive commendation; the chief ministers all praised him, and the emperor said, "Xi keeps to poverty and upholds the Way; his modest withdrawal is worthy of praise."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Kejia memorialized that Zhu Xi had repeatedly been summoned without rising and ought to receive commendation. The chief ministers all praised him, and the emperor said, "Xi keeps to poverty and upholds the Way; his modest withdrawal is worthy of praise."

sentences.zh: 特改合入官，主管台州崇道觀。

translations.literal: He was specially given the rank appropriate to his grade and made superintendent of the Chongdao Temple in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially given the rank appropriate to his grade and made superintendent of the Chongdao Temple in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 熹以求退得進，於義未安，再辭。

translations.literal: Xi felt uneasy in principle at being advanced by seeking withdrawal, and declined again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi felt uneasy in principle at being advanced by seeking withdrawal, and declined again.

sentences.zh: 淳熙元年，始拜命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunxi he at last accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Chunxi era he at last accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 二年，上欲獎用廉退，以勵風俗，龔茂良行丞相事以熹名進，除秘書郎，力辭，且以手書遺茂良，言一時權幸群小，乘間讒毀，乃因熹，再辭，即從其請，主管武夷山沖佑觀。

translations.literal: In the second year the emperor wished to reward and employ the modestly withdrawn to encourage public morals; Gong Maoliang, acting as chief councillor, advanced Xi's name and appointed him Secretarial Attendant; he vigorously declined and sent a handwritten letter to Maoliang saying that petty men in power at the time, seizing their chance, slandered and destroyed others through him; he declined again, and the court granted his request, appointing him superintendent of the Chongyou Temple on Mount Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the emperor wished to reward and employ the modestly withdrawn to encourage public morals. Gong Maoliang, acting as chief councillor, advanced Zhu Xi's name and appointed him secretarial attendant. He vigorously declined and sent a handwritten letter to Maoliang saying that petty men in power at the time, seizing their chance, slandered and destroyed others through him. He declined again, and the court granted his request, appointing him superintendent of the Chongyou Temple on Mount Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 五年，史浩再相，除知南康軍，降旨便道之官，熹再辭，不許。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when Shi Hao again became chief councilor, Xi was appointed military prefect of Nankang; an edict ordered him to proceed by the direct route to office; Xi declined twice and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xiaozong's reign, when Shi Hao returned as chief councilor, Xi was appointed prefect of Nankang; an edict told him to proceed directly to his post, but though he declined twice, the court would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 至郡，興利除害，值歲不雨，講求荒政，多所全活。

translations.literal: On reaching the prefecture he promoted benefit and removed harm; the year brought no rain, and he studied famine administration, saving many lives.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his prefecture he promoted public good and removed abuses; when drought struck that year, he organized famine relief and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 訖事，奏乞依格推賞納粟人。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he memorialized requesting that rewards be granted according to regulation to those who had contributed grain.
translations.idiomatic: When the relief effort ended, he memorialized that those who had contributed grain should receive rewards according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 間詣郡學，引進士子與之講論。

translations.literal: From time to time he went to the prefectural school and led degree-holders in discussion with him.
translations.idiomatic: He also visited the prefectural school from time to time to lecture and debate with the students.

sentences.zh: 訪白鹿洞書院遺址，奏復其舊，為《學規》俾守之。

translations.literal: He sought out the old site of Bailudong Academy, memorialized to restore it, and composed Regulations for Study for its observance.
translations.idiomatic: He located the ruins of Bailudong Academy, memorialized for its restoration, and drew up School Regulations for the academy to follow.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，大旱，詔監司、郡守條其民間利病，遂上疏言：

translations.literal: The next summer there was great drought; an edict ordered intendant-commissioners and prefects to list the benefits and harms affecting the people, and he thereupon submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: The following summer a severe drought struck; the throne ordered intendant-commissioners and prefects to report on local hardships, and Xi submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 天下之務莫大於恤民，而恤民之本，在人君正心術以立紀綱。

translations.literal: Among the tasks of the realm none is greater than cherishing the people, and the root of cherishing the people lies in the ruler rectifying his mind and methods to establish institutions.
translations.idiomatic: No task under Heaven is greater than caring for the people, and the foundation of that care lies in the ruler rectifying his mind and thereby establishing sound institutions.

sentences.zh: 蓋天下之紀綱不能以自立，必人主之心術公平正大，無偏黨反側之私，然後有所繫而立。

translations.literal: For the institutions of the realm cannot stand by themselves; only when the ruler's mind and methods are fair, upright, and great, without partisan or contrary private motives, can they have something to which to attach and thereby be established.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions cannot sustain themselves: only when the ruler's mind is fair, upright, and free of factional or selfish bias can they take root and endure.

sentences.zh: 君心不能以自正，必親賢臣，遠小人，講明義理之歸，閉塞私邪之路，然後乃可得而正。

translations.literal: The ruler's mind cannot rectify itself; he must be close to worthy ministers, keep petty men at a distance, clarify where principle leads, and block the paths of private evil—only then can it be rectified.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's mind cannot correct itself unaided: he must draw near worthy ministers, keep petty men at a distance, study where moral principle leads, and shut off the roads of private corruption—only then can his mind be made right.

sentences.zh: 今宰相、臺省、師傅、賓友、諫諍之臣皆失其職，而陛下所與親密謀議者，不過一二近習之臣。

translations.literal: Today the chief councilor, the censorate, tutors, friends of the heir, and remonstrating ministers have all lost their functions, while those with whom Your Majesty intimately plots are no more than one or two favored attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Today the chief councilor, the censorate, the heir's tutors, his advisers, and remonstrating officials have all been reduced to impotence, while Your Majesty's intimate counselors are no more than one or two favored attendants.

sentences.zh: 上以蠱惑陛下之心志，使陛下不信先王之大道，而說於功利之卑說，不樂莊士之讜言，而安於私暬之鄙態。

translations.literal: Above, they bewitch Your Majesty's mind so that Your Majesty does not trust the great Way of the former kings but is persuaded by base talk of profit and utility, does not delight in the forthright words of upright scholars, but rests content in the vulgar ways of private favorites.
translations.idiomatic: They bewitch Your Majesty's mind from above, leading him to distrust the great Way of the ancient kings, to heed base doctrines of profit and expedience, to reject the frank counsel of upright scholars, and to rest content in the vulgar company of private favorites.

sentences.zh: 下則招集天下士大夫之嗜利無恥者，文武彙分，各入其門。

translations.literal: Below, they gather throughout the realm those literati and officials who crave profit and lack shame; civil and military men are sorted and each enters their gate.
translations.idiomatic: Below, they recruit from across the empire those officials who crave profit and know no shame, sorting civil and military men into separate factions that enter their respective camps.

sentences.zh: 所喜則陰為引援，擢置清顯。

translations.literal: Those they favor they secretly recommend and promote to clear, eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Those they favor they secretly advance to honorable office.

sentences.zh: 所惡則密行訾毀，公肆擠排。

translations.literal: Those they hate they secretly slander and openly drive out.
translations.idiomatic: Those they hate they secretly defame and openly squeeze from office.

sentences.zh: 交通貨賂，所盜者皆陛下之財。

translations.literal: They traffic in bribes; what they steal is all Your Majesty's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: They traffic in bribes, stealing what belongs to the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 命卿置將，所竊者皆陛下之柄。

translations.literal: They order ministers and appoint generals; what they usurp is all Your Majesty's authority.
translations.idiomatic: They appoint ministers and generals, usurping powers that belong to Your Majesty alone.

sentences.zh: 陛下所謂宰相、師傅、賓友、諫諍之臣，或反出入其門牆，承望其風旨；

translations.literal: Those whom Your Majesty calls chief councilor, tutor, friend of the heir, and remonstrating minister in turn pass in and out of their gates and court their intentions;
translations.idiomatic: Those whom Your Majesty calls chief councilor, tutors, advisers, and remonstrators instead pass through their gates and defer to their wishes;

sentences.zh: 其幸能自立者，亦不過齪齪自守，而未嘗敢一言以斥之；

translations.literal: those fortunate enough to stand on their own do no more than fussily guard themselves and have never dared a single word to rebuke them;
translations.idiomatic: those few who manage to stand apart merely fuss over their own integrity and never dare speak a word of rebuke;

sentences.zh: 其甚畏公論者，乃能略警逐其徒黨之一二，既不能深有所傷，而終亦不敢正言以搗其囊橐窟穴之所在。

translations.literal: those who greatly fear public opinion can only slightly warn and drive out one or two of their partisans; they can neither wound them deeply nor in the end dare speak plainly to strike at where their purses and lairs lie.
translations.idiomatic: those who fear public opinion may drive out one or two of their followers, but cannot wound them deeply and still dare not speak plainly against the nests where their wealth and power are hoarded.

sentences.zh: 勢成威立，中外靡然向之，使陛下之號令黜陟不復出於朝廷，而出於一二人之門，名為陛下獨斷，而實此一二人者陰執其柄。

translations.literal: When their power is formed and authority established, inside and outside all turn to them, so that Your Majesty's orders of appointment and dismissal no longer issue from the court but from the gates of one or two men; it is called Your Majesty's sole decision, but in truth these one or two men secretly hold the handle.
translations.idiomatic: Once their power is secure, the whole court defers to them; appointments and dismissals no longer issue from the throne but from the doors of one or two men. Your Majesty is said to decide alone, but in truth these men secretly hold the reins of power.

sentences.zh: 且云：「莫大之禍，必至之憂，近在朝夕，而陛下獨未之知。」

translations.literal: Moreover he said, "The greatest calamity and the worry that must come are close at hand, within days, yet Your Majesty alone does not know it."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "The greatest calamity and the gravest peril are imminent, yet Your Majesty alone remains unaware of them."

sentences.zh: 上讀之，大怒曰：「是以我為亡也。」

translations.literal: When the emperor read it, he was greatly enraged and said, "He takes me for doomed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read this and flew into a rage: "He thinks my dynasty is finished."

sentences.zh: 熹以疾請祠，不報。

translations.literal: Xi requested a temple sinecure on grounds of illness; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Xi asked to be relieved on grounds of illness and given a temple appointment; the court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 陳俊卿以舊相守金陵，過闕入見，薦熹甚力。

translations.literal: Chen Junqing, as a former chief councilor guarding Jinling, passed the capital on his way to audience and recommended Xi with great force.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Junqing, a former chief councilor serving at Jinling, came to court on his way through the capital and strongly recommended Xi.

sentences.zh: 宰相趙雄言於上曰：「士之好名，陛下疾之愈甚，則人之譽之愈眾，無乃適所以高之。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Zhao Xiong said to the emperor, "When a gentleman loves reputation, the more Your Majesty detests it, the more people praise him—might this not be exactly what elevates him?
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Zhao Xiong told the emperor, "When a scholar courts reputation, the more Your Majesty resents it, the more the public praises him—might that not only raise him higher?

sentences.zh: 不若因其長而用之，彼漸當事任，能否自見矣。」

translations.literal: Better to employ him for his strengths; as he gradually takes on duties, whether he can or cannot perform will show of itself."
translations.idiomatic: Better to employ him for his strengths; once he takes on real duties, his capacity will reveal itself."

sentences.zh: 上以為然，乃除熹提舉江西常平茶鹽公事。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right and thereupon appointed Xi Commissioner for the Ever-Normal Granaries and Tea-Salt Monopoly in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and appointed Xi Commissioner for the Ever-Normal Granaries and the Tea and Salt Monopoly in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 旋錄救荒之勞，除直秘閣，以前所奏納粟人未推賞，辭。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward his famine-relief service was recorded and he was made Direct Attendant of the Secretariat; because those who had contributed grain in his earlier memorial had not yet received rewards, he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his famine-relief work was recognized with appointment as Direct Attendant of the Secretariat, but he declined because those who had contributed grain had still not received the rewards he had recommended.

sentences.zh: 會浙東大饑，宰相王淮奏改熹提舉浙東常平茶鹽公事，即日單車就道，復以納粟人未推賞，辭職名。

translations.literal: It happened that eastern Zhejiang suffered great famine; Chief Councilor Wang Huai memorialized to change Xi's appointment to Commissioner for the Ever-Normal Granaries and Tea-Salt Monopoly in eastern Zhejiang; that same day Xi took a single cart and set out on the road, but again because those who had contributed grain had not been rewarded, he declined the title of office.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern Zhejiang suffered severe famine, Chief Councilor Wang Huai had Xi transferred to the same post in that region; Xi set out the same day with only a single cart, but again declined the appointment because the grain contributors had not yet been rewarded.

sentences.zh: 納粟賞行，遂受職名。

translations.literal: When the rewards for contributing grain were carried out, he then accepted the title of office.
translations.idiomatic: Once the grain contributors had been rewarded, he accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 入對，首陳災異之由與修德任人之說，次言：「陛下即政之初，蓋嘗選建英豪，任以政事，不幸其間不能盡得其人，是以不復廣求賢哲，而姑取軟熟易制之人以充其位。

translations.literal: On entering audience he first set forth the causes of strange portents and the doctrine of cultivating virtue and employing men, then said, "At the beginning of Your Majesty's assumption of rule, you broadly selected and established heroic talents and entrusted them with administration; unfortunately among them you could not fully obtain the right men, and therefore you no longer broadly sought worthy sages but for the time took soft, pliable, easily controlled men to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: At court he first explained the causes of portents and urged cultivating virtue and appointing worthy men, then said: "When Your Majesty first took power, you chose outstanding men and entrusted them with government; unfortunately not all proved equal to the task, and thereafter you ceased seeking the truly wise, contenting yourself with pliable men easy to control.

sentences.zh: 於是左右私褻使令之賤，始得以奉燕閒，備驅使，而宰相之權日輕。

translations.literal: Thereupon the base men of private favor on left and right who carried orders were first able to attend at leisurely gatherings and serve as runners, while the chief councilor's power grew daily lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the low attendants of private favor gained access to Your Majesty's leisure hours and came to run errands, while the chief councilor's authority dwindled day by day.

sentences.zh: 又慮其勢有所偏，而因重以壅己也，則時聽外廷之論，將以陰察此輩之負犯而操切之。

translations.literal: Fearing again that their power might lean one way and, by adding weight, block him, he would from time to time heed discussion in the outer court, intending secretly to observe these men's offenses and grasp and control them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing their power might grow one-sided and choke off his own, Your Majesty would sometimes heed outside opinion, intending secretly to catch these men in fault and hold them in check.

sentences.zh: 陛下既未能循天理、公聖心，以正朝廷之大體，則固已失其本矣，而又欲兼聽士大夫之言，以為駕馭之術，則士大夫之進見有時，而近習之從容無間。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, having been unable to follow Heaven's principle and make public the sage mind to rectify the great body of the court, has already lost the root; yet you also wish to heed together the words of literati as a technique of control—then the literati's access to audience is occasional, while the favored attendants' ease is without interval.
translations.idiomatic: Having failed to align the court with Heaven's principle and the sage mind, Your Majesty has already lost the root; yet you also wish to heed literati opinion as a technique of control—yet literati see the throne only occasionally, while favored attendants enjoy unbroken access.

sentences.zh: 士大夫之禮貌既莊而難親，其議論又苦而難入，近習便辟側媚之態既足以蠱心志，其胥史狡獪之術又足以眩聰明。

translations.literal: The literati's deportment is already solemn and hard to be close to, and their discourse bitter and hard to take in; the favored attendants' fawning, obsequious manner is already enough to bewitch the mind, and their clerks' crafty tricks enough to dazzle clear sight.
translations.idiomatic: Literati are formal and hard to approach; their counsel is austere and hard to hear. Favored attendants flatter and bewitch the mind, while their clerks deceive with crafty tricks that cloud Your Majesty's judgment.

sentences.zh: 是以雖欲微抑此輩，而此輩之勢日重，雖欲兼采公論，而士大夫之勢日輕。

translations.literal: Thus although you wish slightly to restrain these men, their power grows daily heavier; although you wish to take in public opinion together, the literati's power grows daily lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Thus although Your Majesty wishes slightly to restrain the favorites, their power grows daily; although he wishes to heed public opinion, the literati grow daily weaker.

sentences.zh: 重者既挾其重，以竊陛下之權，輕者又借力於所重，以為竊位固寵之計。

translations.literal: The heavy already wield their weight to steal Your Majesty's power; the light again borrow strength from the heavy as a plan to steal posts and secure favor.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful use their weight to usurp Your Majesty's authority; the lesser borrow their strength to cling to office and secure favor.

sentences.zh: 日往月來，浸淫耗蝕，使陛下之德業日隳，綱紀日壞，邪佞充塞，貨賂公行，兵愁民怨，盜賊間作，災異數見，饑饉薦臻。

translations.literal: Day by day and month by month, soaking and eroding, they cause Your Majesty's virtue and achievement to decay daily, institutions to worsen daily, the wicked and flatterers to fill the space, bribes to walk openly, soldiers to grieve and the people to resent, bandits to arise at intervals, strange portents to appear repeatedly, and famine to come one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day and month by month this corrodes Your Majesty's virtue, undermines institutions, fills the court with flatterers, spreads bribery openly, leaves soldiers discontent and the people resentful, breeds banditry, multiplies portents, and brings famine upon famine.

sentences.zh: 群小相挻，人人皆得滿其所欲，惟有陛下了無所得，而顧乃獨受其弊。」

translations.literal: The petty men assist one another; each obtains his fill of desire, while Your Majesty alone gains nothing and yet alone bears the harm."
translations.idiomatic: Petty men support one another; each gets what he wants, while Your Majesty alone gains nothing and alone suffers the harm."

sentences.zh: 上為動容。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved in countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 所奏凡七事，其一二事手書以防宣洩。

translations.literal: What he memorialized amounted to seven matters; one or two of them he wrote in his own hand to guard against leakage.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial covered seven points; for one or two of them he wrote out the text in his own hand to prevent leaks.

sentences.zh: 熹始拜命，即移書他郡，募米商，蠲其征，及至，則客舟之米已輻湊。

translations.literal: As soon as Xi first received appointment, he sent letters to other prefectures recruiting grain merchants and remitting their taxes; when he arrived, merchant boats' grain had already converged in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office, Xi wrote to neighboring prefectures inviting grain merchants and exempting their taxes; by the time he arrived, merchant vessels laden with rice had already converged on the region.

sentences.zh: 熹日鉤訪民隱，按行境內，單車屏徒從，所至人不及知。

translations.literal: Xi daily investigated the people's hidden grievances and inspected within his jurisdiction, taking a single cart and dismissing attendants; where he went people did not know in time.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he investigated the people's hidden grievances, touring his jurisdiction alone in a simple cart without attendants, arriving before local officials knew he was coming.

sentences.zh: 郡縣官吏憚其風采，至自引去，所部肅然。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county officials feared his bearing; some even withdrew of themselves, and his jurisdiction was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county officials feared his authority; some resigned of their own accord, and his jurisdiction became notably orderly.

sentences.zh: 凡丁錢、和買、役法、榷酤之政，有不便於民者，悉釐而革之。

translations.literal: Whatever policies among the poll tax, government purchase, corvée law, and monopoly on wine were inconvenient to the people, he entirely examined and reformed.
translations.idiomatic: He revised every policy that burdened the people—poll taxes, government purchases, corvée regulations, and wine monopolies.

sentences.zh: 從救荒之餘，隨事處畫，必為經久之計。

translations.literal: Beyond famine relief, he disposed of each matter as it arose and always made long-term plans.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond emergency relief, he addressed each problem as it arose and always sought lasting solutions.

sentences.zh: 有短熹者，謂其疏於為政，上謂王淮曰：「朱熹政事卻有可觀。」

translations.literal: Some who disparaged Xi said he was remiss in administration; the emperor said to Wang Huai, "Zhu Xi's administration is in fact worth observing."
translations.idiomatic: Critics claimed Zhu Xi was negligent in office, but the emperor told Wang Huai, "Zhu Xi's administration is in fact impressive."

sentences.zh: 熹以前後奏請多所見抑，幸而從者，率稽緩後時，蝗旱相仍，不勝憂憤，復奏言：「為今之計，獨有斷自聖心，沛然發號，責躬求言，然後君臣相戒，痛自省改。

translations.literal: Xi, because his successive memorials were largely suppressed and those fortunately approved were generally delayed beyond the proper time, with locusts and drought following one another, could not bear his worry and indignation and again memorialized, saying, "For the present plan, only to decide from the sage mind itself, issue orders abundantly, blame oneself and seek counsel—then ruler and ministers will warn one another and painfully examine and reform themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Because many of his memorials had been suppressed and even approved measures were implemented too late, while locusts and drought followed one another, Xi could bear it no longer and memorialized again: "The only remedy now is for Your Majesty to decide from his own sacred resolve, issue sweeping orders, blame himself and seek counsel—then ruler and ministers can warn one another and reform in earnest.

sentences.zh: 其次惟有盡出內庫之錢，以供大禮之費為收糴之本，詔戶部免征舊負，詔漕臣依條檢放租稅，詔宰臣沙汰被災路分州軍監司、守臣之無狀者，遴選賢能，責以荒政，庶幾猶足下結人心，消其乘時作亂之意。

translations.literal: Next, only to bring out all the money of the inner treasury and use what is for great ritual expenses as capital for purchasing grain; order the Revenue Bureau to exempt old arrears; order transport commissioners to inspect and release rent and tax according to regulations; order chief ministers to sift out the worthless among intendant-commissioners and prefects in the disaster circuits and select the worthy and able, charging them with famine administration—then perhaps one may still bind the people's hearts below and dispel their intent to take advantage of the moment and rise in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Next, draw on the inner treasury—using even funds set aside for state ritual—as capital to buy grain; order the Revenue Bureau to forgive old tax arrears; order transport officials to remit rents and taxes according to law; order chief ministers to remove incompetent officials in the stricken circuits and appoint capable men to manage famine relief—thus binding the people's loyalty and forestalling rebellion.

sentences.zh: 不然，臣恐所憂者不止於饑殍，而將在於盜賊；

translations.literal: Otherwise, I fear what is to be worried over is not only starving corpses but will lie in bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I fear our worry will be not only starving corpses but bandits;

sentences.zh: 蒙其害者不止于官吏，而上及於國家也。」

translations.literal: those who suffer the harm are not only officials but reach up to the state itself."
translations.idiomatic: and those harmed will be not only local officials but the state itself."

sentences.zh: 知台州唐仲友與王淮同裏為姻家，吏部尚書鄭丙、侍御史張大經交薦之，遷江西提刑，未行。

translations.literal: Tang Zhongyou, prefect of Taizhou, was from the same district as Wang Huai and connected by marriage; Minister of Personnel Zheng Bing and Attending Censor Zhang Dajing jointly recommended him, and he was transferred to Jiangxi as judicial intendant, but had not yet departed.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhongyou, prefect of Taizhou, was a fellow townsman and in-law of Wang Huai; Minister of Personnel Zheng Bing and Attending Censor Zhang Dajing jointly recommended him for promotion to judicial intendant of Jiangxi, though he had not yet taken up the post.

sentences.zh: 熹行部至台，訟仲友者紛然，按得其實，章三上，淮匿不以聞。

translations.literal: When Xi made his inspection circuit to Taizhou, those who sued Zhongyou were numerous; on investigation the facts were obtained, and he submitted memorials three times; Huai concealed them and did not report them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi toured Taizhou, lawsuits against Tang Zhongyou poured in; his investigation confirmed the charges, and Xi memorialized three times, but Wang Huai suppressed the reports.

sentences.zh: 熹論愈力，仲友亦自辯，淮乃以熹章進呈，上令宰屬看詳，都司陳庸等乞令浙西提刑委清強官究實，仍令熹速往旱傷州郡相視。

translations.literal: Xi's argument grew stronger; Zhongyou also defended himself; Huai then presented Xi's memorial to the throne; the emperor ordered the chief ministers' staff to examine it in detail; Chen Yong and others of the Palace Secretariat requested that the judicial intendant of western Zhejiang commission a clear, strong official to verify the facts, and still ordered Xi to hurry to drought-stricken prefectures to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Xi pressed his case harder; Tang Zhongyou defended himself; Wang Huai finally submitted Xi's memorial; the emperor ordered the chief ministers' staff to review it; Chen Yong and others asked the judicial intendant of western Zhejiang to send a capable official to investigate, while ordering Xi to hurry to drought-stricken prefectures.

sentences.zh: 熹時留台未行，既奉詔，益上章論，前後六上，淮不得已，奪仲友江西新命以授熹，辭不拜，遂歸，且乞奉祠。

translations.literal: Xi was then staying at Taizhou and had not departed; having received the edict, he further memorialized in argument, six times in all before and after; Huai had no choice but to strip Zhongyou of his new Jiangxi appointment and give it to Xi; Xi declined to accept and returned home, also requesting a temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was still at Taizhou when the edict arrived; he memorialized six times in all; Wang Huai finally revoked Tang Zhongyou's Jiangxi appointment and offered it to Xi, but Xi declined, returned home, and asked for a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 時鄭丙上疏詆程氏之學以沮熹，淮又擢太府寺丞陳賈為監察御史。

translations.literal: At this time Zheng Bing submitted a memorial slandering the learning of the Cheng school to obstruct Xi; Huai also promoted Chen Jia, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zheng Bing memorialized against the Cheng school of learning to block Xi; Wang Huai also promoted Chen Jia of the Imperial Treasury to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 賈面對，首論近日搢紳有所謂「道學」者，大率假名以濟偽，願考察其人，擯棄勿用。

translations.literal: Jia, on facing the throne, first discussed those among recent gentry and officials called "Dao Learning," who for the most part borrow the name to advance falsity, and prayed that such men be investigated and rejected from employment.
translations.idiomatic: In his audience Chen Jia attacked the so-called "Learning of the Way" among recent officials, declaring that most used the name to cover hypocrisy, and urged that such men be investigated and barred from office.

sentences.zh: 蓋指熹也。

translations.literal: This was directed at Xi.
translations.idiomatic: This was aimed at Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔以熹累乞奉祠，可差主管台州崇道觀，既而連奉雲臺、鴻慶之祠者五年。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, an edict said that because Xi had repeatedly requested a temple sinecure, he might be assigned to supervise the Chongdao Temple in Taizhou; thereafter he held the Yuntai and Hongqing temple sinecures in succession for five years.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year an edict granted his repeated requests and assigned him to the Chongdao Temple in Taizhou; he then held successive sinecures at Yuntai and Hongqing temples for five years.

sentences.zh: 十四年，周必大相，除熹提點江西刑獄公事，以疾辭，不許，遂行。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when Zhou Bida became chief councilor, Xi was appointed Judicial Intendant of Jiangxi; he declined on grounds of illness but was not permitted, and thereupon set out.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when Zhou Bida became chief councilor, Xi was appointed Judicial Intendant of Jiangxi; though he pleaded illness, the court refused, and he took up the post.

sentences.zh: 十五年，淮罷相，遂入奏，首言近年刑獄失當，獄官當擇其人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when Huai left the chief ministership, Xi entered and memorialized, first saying that in recent years criminal cases had been mishandled and prison officials should be chosen for their persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, after Wang Huai left office, Xi came to court and memorialized first that recent criminal justice had been mishandled and that prison officials must be carefully chosen.

sentences.zh: 次言經總製錢之病民，及江西諸州科罰之弊。

translations.literal: Next he spoke of how the comprehensive management funds harmed the people and of the abuses of fines and penalties in the prefectures of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He next described how the comprehensive management funds oppressed the people and how arbitrary fines plagued the prefectures of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 而其末言：「陛下即位二十七年，因循荏苒，無尺寸之效可以仰酬聖志。

translations.literal: At the end he said, "Your Majesty has been on the throne twenty-seven years, proceeding by inertia as time passes, with not the slightest effect by which to repay upward the sage will.
translations.idiomatic: He concluded: "Your Majesty has reigned twenty-seven years, yet through inertia and delay has achieved nothing by which to fulfill the founding sage's intent.

sentences.zh: 嘗反覆思之，無乃燕閑蠖濩之中，虛明應物之地，天理有所未純，人欲有所未盡，是以為善不能充其量，除惡不能去其根，一念之頃，公私邪正、是非得失之機，交戰於其中。

translations.literal: I have repeatedly pondered it: perhaps amid leisurely ease and minute stirring, in the place of empty clarity responding to things, Heaven's principle is not wholly pure and human desire is not wholly exhausted; therefore in doing good one cannot fill the measure, in removing evil one cannot uproot it; in the space of a single thought, the mechanisms of public and private, crooked and straight, right and wrong, gain and loss, battle within.
translations.idiomatic: I have pondered this repeatedly: perhaps in moments of leisure, in the mind's empty clarity as it responds to affairs, Heaven's principle is not wholly pure and human desire not wholly subdued; thus good deeds fall short of their full measure and evil is never uprooted; in a single thought public and private, right and wrong, gain and loss contend within the heart.

sentences.zh: 故體貌大臣非不厚，而便嬖側媚得以深被腹心之寄；

translations.literal: Therefore though the outward treatment of great ministers is not ungenerous, favored minions and flatterers are able deeply to receive the trust of the inner heart;
translations.idiomatic: Thus although great ministers are honored in appearance, favored flatterers win the deepest trust of Your Majesty's heart;

sentences.zh: 寤寐英豪非不切，而柔邪庸繆得以久竊廊廟之權。

translations.literal: Sleeping and waking, heroes are not unkeenly sought, yet the soft, corrupt, mediocre, and wrong are able long to usurp hall-and-temple power.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty yearns for heroes awake and asleep, the soft, corrupt, and mediocre have long usurped power at court.

sentences.zh: 非不樂聞公議正論，而有時不容；

translations.literal: It is not that one does not delight to hear public discussion and upright discourse, yet there are times when it is not tolerated;
translations.idiomatic: You do not disdain public debate and honest counsel, yet at times such voices are not tolerated;

sentences.zh: 非不堲讒說殄行，而未免誤聽；

translations.literal: It is not that one does not punish slanderous talk and exterminate misconduct, yet one cannot avoid listening mistakenly;
translations.idiomatic: You do not fail to punish slander and root out misconduct, yet You sometimes heed the wrong voices;

sentences.zh: 非不欲報復陵廟仇恥，而未免畏怯苟安；

translations.literal: It is not that one does not wish to avenge the ancestral halls' enmity and shame, yet one cannot avoid fear, cowardice, and clinging to peace;
translations.idiomatic: You do not lack the will to avenge the insult to the imperial tombs, yet You shrink from action and settle for a precarious peace;

sentences.zh: 非不愛養生靈財力，而未免歎息愁怨。

translations.literal: It is not that one does not love to nurture the people and state finances, yet one cannot avoid sighing over sorrow and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: You care for the people and the treasury, yet You must sigh over their burden and bitterness.

sentences.zh: 願陛下自今以往，一念之頃必謹而察之：此為天理耶，人欲耶？

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty from now on, in the span of a single thought, will always be careful and examine: is this Heaven's principle, or human desire?
translations.idiomatic: I pray that henceforth Your Majesty, in every passing thought, scrutinize carefully: Is this Heaven's principle, or human desire?

sentences.zh: 果天理也，則敬以充之，而不使其少有壅閼；

translations.literal: If it proves to be Heaven's principle, then with reverence fill it out, and do not allow it the slightest obstruction;
translations.idiomatic: If it is Heaven's principle, then with reverence nurture it and permit no obstruction;

sentences.zh: 果人欲也，則敬以克之，而不使其少有凝滯。

translations.literal: If it proves to be human desire, then with reverence overcome it, and do not allow it the slightest lingering.
translations.idiomatic: If it is human desire, then with reverence subdue it and permit no foothold.

sentences.zh: 推而至於言語動作之間，用人處事之際，無不以是裁之，則聖心洞然，中外融澈，無一毫之私欲得以介乎其間，而天下之事將惟陛下所欲為，無不如志矣。」

translations.literal: Extending this to speech and action, to the employing of men and handling of affairs, judging all by this standard, then the sage heart will be luminous, inside and outside will be clear and fused, not a hair of private desire will be able to interpose, and affairs under Heaven will be whatever Your Majesty wishes to do, none not as intended."
translations.idiomatic: Extend this scrutiny to every word and deed, every appointment and decision, and the imperial mind will become luminous and transparent, no private desire able to intrude; then all affairs under Heaven will go as Your Majesty wishes."

sentences.zh: 是行也，有要之於路，以為「正心誠意」之論上所厭聞，戒勿以為言。

translations.literal: On this journey someone waylaid him on the road, thinking the discourse on "rectifying the heart and making intentions sincere" was what the emperor was weary of hearing, and warned him not to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: On this journey someone intercepted him on the road, warning that the emperor had grown weary of hearing about "rectifying the heart and making intentions sincere," and urging him not to raise the topic.

sentences.zh: 熹曰：「吾平生所學，惟此四字，豈可隱默以欺吾君乎？」

translations.literal: Xi said, "All my life's learning amounts to these four characters—how could I keep silent and deceive my lord?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi replied, "All I have learned in my life comes down to these four words—how could I keep silent and deceive my sovereign?"

sentences.zh: 及奏，上曰：「久不見卿，浙東之事，朕自知之，今當處卿清要，不復以州縣為煩也。」

translations.literal: When he presented his memorial, the emperor said, "It has been long since I saw you. As for affairs in eastern Zhe, I know them myself. Now I shall place you in a clear and important post and no longer burden you with prefectures and counties."
translations.idiomatic: When he presented his memorial, the emperor said, "It has been long since we met. I know the situation in eastern Zhe myself. I shall now give you a prestigious central appointment and no longer trouble you with local posts."

sentences.zh: 時曾覿已死，王抃亦逐，獨內侍甘昪尚在，熹力以為言。

translations.literal: At this time Zeng Di was already dead and Wang Bian had also been expelled; only the inner attendant Gan Sheng remained, and Xi pressed the point forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zeng Di was dead and Wang Bian had been driven out; only the inner attendant Gan Sheng remained, and Zhu Xi spoke out against him with force.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「昪乃德壽所薦，謂其有才耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Sheng was recommended by Degao, who said only that he had talent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Gan Sheng was recommended by the Retired Emperor at Degao Palace, who said merely that he had ability."

sentences.zh: 熹曰：「小人無才，安能動人主。」

translations.literal: Xi said, "Petty men have no talent—how could they move the lord of men?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi replied, "Petty men have no talent—how else could they sway the ruler?"

sentences.zh: 翌日，除兵部郎官，以足疾丐祠。

translations.literal: The next day he was appointed Vice Director in the Bureau of Personnel, but on account of foot ailment requested a temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was appointed Vice Director in the Bureau of Personnel, but pleaded foot ailment and requested a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 本部侍郎林栗嘗與熹論《易》、《西銘》不合，劾熹：「本無學術，徒竊張載、程頤緒餘，謂之『道學』。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Lin Li, having once disputed with Xi over the Book of Changes and Western Inscription without agreement, impeached Xi: "He originally had no learning, but merely stole the leftover threads of Zhang Zai and Cheng Yi, calling it 'Learning of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Lin Li, who had once quarreled with Zhu Xi over the Book of Changes and the Western Inscription, impeached him: "He has no real learning of his own, but merely pilfered scraps from Zhang Zai and Cheng Yi and called it the 'Learning of the Way.

sentences.zh: 所至輒攜門生數十人，妄希孔、孟歷聘之風，邀索高價，不肯供職，其偽不可掩。」

translations.literal: Wherever he went he would bring dozens of disciples, vainly hoping to imitate the style of Confucius and Mencius traveling from state to state; he demanded high fees and refused to perform his duties—the falsity cannot be concealed."
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he goes he drags along dozens of disciples, pretentiously imitating Confucius and Mencius on their rounds of appointment, demands lavish payment, and shirks official duty—his hypocrisy cannot be hidden."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「林栗言似過。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Lin Li's words seem excessive."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Lin Li's words seem to go too far."

sentences.zh: 周必大言熹上殿之日，足疾未瘳，勉強登對。

translations.literal: Zhou Bida said that on the day Xi came to court, his foot ailment had not healed and he had forced himself to ascend and respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bida noted that on the day Zhu Xi came to court his foot ailment had not healed and he had forced himself to attend.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕亦見其跛曳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I also saw him limping."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I saw him limping as well."

sentences.zh: 左補闕薛叔似亦奏援熹，乃令依舊職江西提刑。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Official Xue Shousi also memorialized in support of Xi, and he was ordered to retain his original post as Judicial Intendant of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Left Remonstrance Official Xue Shousi also memorialized in Zhu Xi's support, and the court ordered him to resume his former post as Judicial Intendant of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 太常博士葉適上疏與栗辨，謂其言無一實者，「謂之道學」一語，無實尤甚，往日王淮表裏臺諫，陰廢正人，蓋用此術。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ye Shi submitted a memorial disputing with Li, saying that not one of his charges was true; the phrase "called Learning of the Way" was especially groundless—in former days Wang Huai coordinated with censorial and remonstrance officials to secretly remove upright men, and this was the very tactic used.
translations.idiomatic: Court Erudite Ye Shi submitted a memorial rebutting Lin Li, declaring every charge false and the label "Learning of the Way" especially baseless; he noted that Wang Huai had once worked through censorial and remonstrance officials to quietly purge upright men by this same tactic.

sentences.zh: 詔：「熹昨入對，所論皆新任職事，朕諒其誠，復從所請，可疾速之任。」

translations.literal: An edict said, "When Xi entered for audience yesterday, all he discussed concerned new duties; I recognize his sincerity and again grant his request—he should quickly proceed to his post."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "When Zhu Xi came to audience yesterday, he spoke only of his new duties. I trust his sincerity and again grant his request; let him proceed quickly to his post."

sentences.zh: 會胡晉臣除侍御史，首論栗執拗不通，喜同惡異，無事而指學者為黨，乃黜栗知泉州。

translations.literal: When Hu Jinchen was appointed Remonstrance and Examination Official, he first criticized Li as stubborn and uncomprehending, fond of agreeing with the wicked and hating the different, and needlessly calling scholars a faction—Li was then demoted to prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Jinchen was appointed Remonstrance and Examination Official, he opened by attacking Lin Li as obstinate and narrow-minded, eager to side with the wicked and ostracize the unlike-minded, and for no cause branding scholars as a faction; Lin Li was then demoted to prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 熹再辭免，除直寶文閣，主管西京嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: Xi again declined; he was appointed Direct Associate in the Hall of Literary Glory, supervising the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi declined again and was appointed Direct Associate in the Hall of Literary Glory, supervising the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 未逾月再召，熹又辭。

translations.literal: Within a month he was summoned again; Xi again declined.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was summoned again, and Zhu Xi declined once more.

sentences.zh: 始，熹嘗以為口陳之說有所未盡，乞具封事以聞，至是投匭進封事曰：

translations.literal: At first Xi had thought his oral presentation still left something unsaid and had requested to submit a sealed memorial; at this point he placed it in the memorial box and submitted a sealed memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu Xi had felt his oral presentation incomplete and had asked to submit a sealed memorial; now he placed one in the memorial box, writing:

sentences.zh: 今天下大勢，如人有重病，內自心腹，外達四支，無一毛一髮不受病者。

translations.literal: Today the great trend of the empire is like a person with grave illness: from the heart and belly inward, reaching the four limbs outward—not a hair or strand escapes affliction.
translations.idiomatic: The empire today is like a man gravely ill: from heart and belly within to the four limbs without, not a hair is free of disease.

sentences.zh: 且以天下之大本與今日之急務，為陛下言之：大本者，陛下之心；

translations.literal: Let me speak to Your Majesty of the empire's great foundation and today's urgent tasks: the great foundation is Your Majesty's heart;
translations.idiomatic: Let me address Your Majesty on the empire's fundamental root and today's urgent tasks: the fundamental root is Your Majesty's heart;

sentences.zh: 急務則輔翼太子，選任大臣，振舉綱紀，變化風俗，愛養民力，修明軍政，六者是也。

translations.literal: The urgent tasks are assisting the crown prince, selecting great ministers, revitalizing norms and institutions, transforming customs, cherishing the people's strength, and repairing military government—these six.
translations.idiomatic: The urgent tasks are assisting the crown prince, selecting great ministers, restoring discipline, reforming customs, conserving the people's strength, and strengthening military administration—these six.

sentences.zh: 古先聖王兢兢業業，持守此心，是以建師保之官，列諫諍之職，凡飲食、酒漿、衣服、次舍、器用、財賄與夫宦官、宮妾之政，無一不領於冢宰。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings, cautious and reverent, held fast to this heart; therefore they established tutor-and-protector offices and lined up remonstrance duties; food, drink, wine, soup, clothing, lodging, utensils, wealth and gifts, and the administration of eunuchs and palace women—all were overseen by the chief steward.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sage kings guarded this heart with tireless care; they established tutor-and-protector offices and remonstrance posts; food, drink, clothing, lodging, goods, gifts, and even the management of eunuchs and palace women—all fell under the chief steward's oversight.

sentences.zh: 使其左右前後，一動一靜，無不制以有司之法，而無纖芥之隙、瞬息之頃，得以隱其毫髮之私。

translations.literal: Thus before and behind them, to left and right, every movement and stillness was regulated by official law, without the slightest gap or moment in which to hide the least private selfishness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus every movement around them, every moment of stillness, was governed by official regulation, leaving not the smallest opening or instant in which private desire could hide.

sentences.zh: 陛下所以精一克復而持守其心，果有如此之功乎？

translations.literal: The means by which Your Majesty through refinement and singleness overcomes and holds fast to the heart—does it truly have such achievement?
translations.idiomatic: Has Your Majesty, through refinement and singleness of mind, truly achieved such mastery in holding fast to the heart?

sentences.zh: 所以修身齊家而正其左右，果有如此之效乎？

translations.literal: The means by which Your Majesty cultivates the self and orders the family and corrects those at your side—does it truly have such effect?
translations.idiomatic: Has Your Majesty truly achieved such results in self-cultivation, household order, and correcting those at your side?

sentences.zh: 宮省事禁，臣固不得而知，然爵賞之濫，貨賂之流，閭巷竊言，久已不勝其籍籍，則陛下所以修之家者，恐其未有以及古之聖王也。

translations.literal: Palace affairs and restrictions—I cannot know—but the indiscriminate granting of ranks and rewards, the flow of bribes, and whispers in alleys have long been unbearably rife; then Your Majesty's efforts to cultivate the household probably have not yet reached the ancient sage kings.
translations.idiomatic: Palace affairs are hidden from me, yet the reckless bestowal of honors, the traffic in bribes, and street gossip have long been rampant; Your Majesty's governance of the household has surely not yet matched that of the ancient sage kings.

sentences.zh: 至於左右便嬖之私，恩遇過當，往者淵、覿、說、抃之徒勢焰熏灼，傾動一時，今已無可言矣。

translations.literal: As for private favor toward attendants at your side and excessive grace—formerly Yuan, Di, Shuo, Bian, and their like had blinding influence and swayed their age; now there is nothing left to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: As for undue favor toward personal attendants: men such as Yuan, Di, Shuo, and Wang Bian once wielded blinding power and swayed the age, but of them there is nothing left to say.

sentences.zh: 獨有前日臣所面陳者，雖蒙聖慈委曲開譬，然臣之愚，竊以為此輩但當使之守門傳命，供掃除之役，不當假借崇長，使得逞邪媚、作淫巧於內，以蕩上心，立門庭、招權勢於外，以累聖政。

translations.literal: Only the man I faced and stated before—though I received the imperial grace of roundabout consolation—yet in my stupidity I privately think these people should only be made to guard gates, transmit orders, and perform sweeping duties; they should not be lent lofty advancement, allowed to practice flattery and wicked craft within to unsettle the imperial heart, or establish private gates and gather power without to burden sagely government.
translations.idiomatic: Only the man I raised before Your Majesty remains; though the throne answered with gentle reassurance, I still believe such men should merely guard gates, carry messages, and sweep floors—not be elevated to power, practicing flattery and intrigue within to sway the imperial mind and building private networks without to burden the government.

sentences.zh: 臣聞之道路，自王抃既逐之後，諸將差除，多出此人之手。

translations.literal: I hear on the roads that since Wang Bian was expelled, most appointments and removals of generals have passed through this man's hands.
translations.idiomatic: I hear from travelers that since Wang Bian's expulsion, most appointments and dismissals of generals have passed through this man's hands.

sentences.zh: 陛下竭生靈膏血以奉軍旅，顧乃未嘗得一溫飽，是皆將帥巧為名色，奪取其糧，肆行貨賂于近習，以圖進用，出入禁闥腹心之臣，外交將帥，共為欺蔽，以至於此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty exhausts the people's lifeblood to supply the armies, yet they never receive even a full meal—this is because commanders craftily make pretexts, seize their rations, and freely bribe favorites to seek advancement; inner attendants who enter and leave the forbidden gates, who are trusted as close to the heart, maintain outward ties with generals and together practice deception, until it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty drains the people's lifeblood to feed the armies, yet the soldiers never know a full meal—because commanders invent pretexts, seize their rations, and bribe Your Majesty's favorites to win promotion; trusted inner attendants who traffic with generals conspire in deception until matters have reached this pass.

sentences.zh: 而陛下不悟，反寵暱之，以是為我之私人，至使宰相不得議其制置之得失，給諫不得論其除授之是非，則陛下所以正其左右者，未能及古之聖王又明矣。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty does not perceive it, but on the contrary favors and is intimate with him, taking him as your private man, so that the chief councilor cannot discuss the merits of his appointment and remonstrance officials cannot debate the right and wrong of his selection—then Your Majesty's means of correcting those at your side clearly have not yet reached the ancient sage kings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty does not see this, but instead favors him as a personal retainer, so that the chief councilor cannot judge his appointment and remonstrance officials cannot challenge his selection—making it plain that Your Majesty has not yet corrected those at your side as the ancient sage kings did.

sentences.zh: 至於輔翼太子，則自王十朋、陳良翰之後，宮僚之選號為得人，而能稱其職者，蓋已鮮矣。

translations.literal: As for assisting the crown prince, since Wang Shipeng and Chen Lianghan, the palace staff selections were said to have obtained the right men, yet those able to fulfill their duties were already few.
translations.idiomatic: As for assisting the crown prince: since Wang Shipeng and Chen Lianghan, the palace staff were said to have been well chosen, yet few who could truly perform their duties remained.

sentences.zh: 而又時使邪佞儇薄、闒冗庸妄之輩，或得參錯於其間，所謂講讀，亦姑以應文備數，而未聞其有箴規之效。

translations.literal: Furthermore, at times wicked, frivolous, vulgar, and mediocre types are mixed in; so-called lecturing and reading is merely perfunctory to fulfill numbers, and one does not hear of any admonitory effect.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, wicked, frivolous, and mediocre men are sometimes intermixed among them; the so-called lectures are mere formalities to fill quotas, and one hears of no real admonition.

sentences.zh: 至於從容朝夕、陪侍遊燕者，又不過使臣宦者數輩而已。

translations.literal: Those who accompany him at leisure morning and evening, attending at banquets and excursions, are no more than a few palace attendants and eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Those who keep him company at leisure, morning and evening, at banquets and outings, are no more than a handful of palace attendants and eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 師傅、賓客既不復置，而詹事、庶子有名無實，其左右春坊遂直以使臣掌之，既無以發其隆師親友、尊德樂義之心，又無以防其戲慢媟狎、奇邪雜進之害。

translations.literal: Tutor and guest offices were no longer established; chamberlain and sub-chamberlain posts were empty in name; the attendants of the Eastern Palace were directly managed by envoys—there was no means to awaken his heart to honor teachers, cherish friends, revere virtue, and delight in righteousness, nor any means to guard against the harm of playful disrespect, improper familiarity, and the entry of strange and wicked influences.
translations.idiomatic: The tutor and guest offices were abolished; the chamberlain and sub-chamberlain were titles without substance; the crown prince's attendants were placed directly under palace envoys—so that neither could he be moved to honor teachers and delight in virtue, nor could he be shielded from disrespect, improper intimacy, and the intrusion of corrupt influences.

sentences.zh: 宜討論前典，置師傅、賓客之官，罷去春坊使臣，而使詹事、庶子各復其職。

translations.literal: One should consult former regulations, establish tutor and guest offices, remove Eastern Palace envoys, and restore chamberlain and sub-chamberlain to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should consult ancient precedent, restore the tutor and guest offices, abolish the Eastern Palace envoys, and return the chamberlain and sub-chamberlain to their proper functions.

sentences.zh: 至於選任大臣，則以陛下之聰明，豈不知天下之事，必得剛明公正之人而後可任哉？

translations.literal: As for selecting great ministers—with Your Majesty's intelligence, do you not know that affairs under Heaven must be entrusted to firm, bright, and impartial men before they can be borne?
translations.idiomatic: As for selecting great ministers: with Your Majesty's intelligence, do You not know that the empire's affairs can be entrusted only to men who are resolute, clear-sighted, and impartial?

sentences.zh: 其所以常不得如此之人，而反容鄙夫之竊位者，直以一念之間，未能徹其私邪之蔽，而燕私之好，便嬖之流，不能盡由於法度，若用剛明公正之人以為輔相，則恐其有以妨吾之事，害吾之人，而不得肆。

translations.literal: The reason one often cannot get such men, but instead tolerates vulgar fellows usurping position, is directly that for a moment one fails utterly to pierce the obscuring of private wickedness; private banquet pleasures and favored minions cannot wholly be constrained by law—if firm, bright, and impartial men were used as chief ministers, one fears they would obstruct our affairs and harm our people and not be allowed to run riot.
translations.idiomatic: The reason such men are rarely chosen and vulgar placeholders hold office is that private desire still clouds the mind; private indulgence and favored minions cannot be fully bound by law. Firm, impartial ministers would obstruct private affairs and restrain private men—and so they are feared.

sentences.zh: 是以選擇之際，常先排擯此等，而後取凡疲懦軟熟、平日不敢直言正色之人而揣摩之，又於其中得其至庸極陋、決可保其不至於有所妨者，然後舉而加之於位。

translations.literal: Therefore at the time of selection one first excludes such men, then takes from among the worn, cowardly, soft, and seasoned—those who ordinarily dare not speak straight or show stern countenance—and feels them out; then from among those finds the most mediocre and base, those certain not to obstruct anything, and only then raises and puts them in office.
translations.idiomatic: At selection time such men are first excluded; then from among the timid, pliable, and seasoned—those who dare not speak plainly—candidates are tested; and from these the most mediocre and harmless are chosen and elevated to office.

sentences.zh: 是以除書未出，而物色先定，姓名未顯，而中外已逆知其決非天下第一流矣。

translations.literal: Therefore before the appointment edict issues, the target is already fixed; before the name appears, inside and outside already know in advance that it will certainly not be the world's foremost rank.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the choice is settled before the appointment edict is issued, and court and country alike know in advance that the appointee will certainly not be a man of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 至於振肅紀綱，變化風俗，則今日宮省之間，禁密之地，而天下不公之道，不正之人，顧乃得以窟穴盤據於其間。

translations.literal: As for invigorating discipline and transforming customs—in today's palace precincts, the most restricted zone—yet the empire's unjust ways and unrighteous men are able to burrow and entrench there.
translations.idiomatic: As for restoring discipline and reforming customs: in the palace itself, the most guarded of places, the empire's injustice and unworthy men are allowed to nest and entrench.

sentences.zh: 而陛下目見耳聞，無非不公不正之事，則其所以熏烝銷鑠，使陛下好善之心不著，疾惡之意不深，其害已有不可勝言者矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's eyes see and ears hear nothing but unjust and unrighteous affairs; then their fumigating and melting make Your Majesty's heart for the good not manifest and hatred of evil not deep—the harm is already beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty sees and hears is nothing but injustice; such an atmosphere erodes the love of good and dulls the hatred of evil—the harm is already beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 及其作姦犯法，則陛下又未能深割私愛，而付諸外廷之議，論以有司之法，是以紀綱不正於上，風俗頹弊於下，其為患之日久矣。

translations.literal: When they commit treachery and violate law, Your Majesty again cannot deeply cut private affection and hand them to outer court deliberation, judged by official law—thus norms are not upright above and customs decay below; the harm has been long.
translations.idiomatic: When they break the law, Your Majesty again cannot set aside private affection and leave them to the outer court and the law—so discipline fails above and morals decay below; the harm has been long in the making.

sentences.zh: 而浙中為尤甚。

translations.literal: And in Zhejiang it is especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: The condition is especially grave in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 大率習為軟美之態、依阿之言，以不分是非不辨曲直為得計，甚者以金珠為脯醢，以契券為詩文，宰相可啖則啖宰相，近習可通則通近習，惟得之求，無復廉恥。

translations.literal: Generally they habituate to soft, flattering demeanor and equivocating speech, taking not distinguishing right from wrong and not distinguishing crooked from straight as good policy; worse, they treat gold and pearls as preserved meats and bonds as poetry and prose; if the chief councilor can be fed, feed the chief councilor; if favorites can be reached, reach the favorites—only seeking to obtain, no longer knowing shame.
translations.idiomatic: Men there cultivate a manner of soft flattery and evasive speech, treating indifference to right and wrong as shrewdness; worse still, they offer gold and pearls as gifts and contracts as literary tokens—bribing the chief councilor when they can, cultivating favorites when they must—seeking gain without shame.

sentences.zh: 一有剛毅正直、守道循理之士出乎其間，則群譏眾排，指為「道學」，而加以矯激之罪。

translations.literal: Once a firm, upright man who keeps to the Way and follows principle appears among them, the crowd mocks and collectively expels him, calling him "Learning of the Way," and adds the crime of excessive rigidity.
translations.idiomatic: When a resolute, upright man devoted to principle appears among them, the crowd mocks and drives him out, branding him with "Learning of the Way" and charging him with excessive rigidity.

sentences.zh: 十數年來，以此二字禁錮天下之賢人君子，復如昔時所謂元祐學術者，排擯詆辱，必使無所容其身而後已，此豈治世之事哉？

translations.literal: For more than ten years, using these two characters they have imprisoned the empire's worthy men and gentlemen—again like the former so-called Yuanyou learning faction, excluding and reviling until they have nowhere to stand—how can this be the affair of an orderly age?
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years these two words have been used to confine the empire's worthy men—just as in the old Yuanyou learning purges, hounding them until they have no place to stand. Is this the way of a well-governed age?

sentences.zh: 至於愛養民力，修明軍政，則自虞允文之為相也，盡取版曹歲入窠名之必可指擬者，號為歲終羨餘之數，而輸之內帑。

translations.literal: As for cherishing the people's strength and repairing military government—since Yu Yunwen was chief councilor, he took all identifiable revenue items of the Ministry of Revenue's annual income, called them year-end surplus figures, and submitted them to the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: As for conserving the people's strength and strengthening the military: when Yu Yunwen was chief councilor, he identified every fixed revenue item in the Ministry of Revenue's annual intake, labeled the total year-end surplus, and diverted it to the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 顧以其有名無實、積累掛欠、空載簿籍、不可催理者，撥還版曹，以為內帑之積，將以備他日用兵進取不時之須。

translations.literal: Yet those with name but no reality, piled-up arrears, and empty ledger entries that cannot be collected he transferred back to the Ministry of Revenue as inner treasury reserves, to prepare for unforeseen future military needs.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile unreal entries, accumulated arrears, and uncollectable accounts on the books were shifted back to the Ministry of Revenue as inner reserves, supposedly to fund future military campaigns.

sentences.zh: 然自是以來二十餘年，內帑歲入不知幾何，而認為私貯，典以私人，宰相不得以式貢均節其出入，版曹不得以簿書勾考其在亡，日銷月耗，以奉燕私之費者，蓋不知其幾何矣，而曷嘗聞其能用此錢以易敵人之首，如太祖之言哉。
