translations.literal: But from then for more than twenty years, inner treasury annual intake—who knows how much?—is treated as private stores and managed by private men; the chief councilor cannot use tribute formulas to balance income and outgo; the Ministry of Revenue cannot use ledgers to verify presence or absence; daily and monthly it is consumed for private banquet expenses—who knows how much?—yet when has one heard of using this money to buy enemy heads, as Taizu spoke?
translations.idiomatic: Yet for more than twenty years since, the inner treasury's annual intake—who knows how much?—has been hoarded as private wealth and managed by private hands; the chief councilor cannot regulate its flow, nor the Ministry audit its accounts. It is spent daily on private indulgence—yet when has it been used, as Taizu said it should be, to buy the heads of enemies?

sentences.zh: 徒使版曹經費闕乏日甚，督促日峻，以至廢去祖宗以來破分良法，而必以十分登足為限；

translations.literal: In vain the Ministry of Revenue's operating funds grow daily deficient and supervision grows daily harsh, to the point of abolishing the good apportionment methods since the ancestors and insisting on full ten-tenths collection as the limit;
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue's operating funds grow ever scarcer while exactions grow ever harsher, until the apportionment methods of the founders were abolished and full collection to the last fraction was enforced;

sentences.zh: 以為未足，則又造為比較監司、郡守殿最之法，以誘脅之。

translations.literal: deeming it insufficient, they further created comparison methods for circuit intendants and prefects' performance rankings to induce and coerce.
translations.idiomatic: and finding even that insufficient, comparison rankings for circuit intendants and prefects were devised to coerce compliance.

sentences.zh: 於是中外承風，競為苛急，此民力之所以重困也。

translations.literal: Thus inside and outside follow the wind, competing in harsh urgency—this is why the people's strength is doubly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike took up harsh urgency in competition—this is why the people's strength has been so grievously exhausted.

sentences.zh: 諸將之求進也，必先掊克士卒，以殖私利，然後以此自結于陛下之私人，而蘄以姓名達于陛下之貴將。

translations.literal: When generals seek advancement, they must first squeeze the soldiers to grow private profit, then use this to attach themselves to Your Majesty's private men, hoping their names reach Your Majesty's honored generals.
translations.idiomatic: Generals seeking promotion must first squeeze their troops for private gain, then use the proceeds to cultivate Your Majesty's favorites, hoping their names will reach the senior commanders.

sentences.zh: 貴將得其姓名，即以付之軍中，使自什伍以上節次保明，稱其材武堪任將帥，然後具奏牘而言之陛下之前。

translations.literal: The honored generals get their names and hand them to the army, having ranks from squad leaders upward certify step by step, praising their talent and martial bearing as fit for command, then submit memorials stating this before Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The senior commanders receive these names, pass them to the army for certification rank by rank from squad leaders upward, attest to their fitness for command, and then memorialize Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下但見等級推先，案牘具備，則誠以為公薦而可以得人矣，而豈知其諧價輸錢，已若晚唐之債帥哉？

translations.literal: Your Majesty only sees ranks advancing in order and documents complete, then truly believes it public recommendation that can obtain men—how do you know they negotiated prices and paid money, already like Late Tang debt-commanders?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sees orderly ranks and complete paperwork and believes it honest recommendation—how would You know they have haggled over prices and paid bribes, like the debt-bought commanders of late Tang?

sentences.zh: 夫將者，三軍之司命，而其選置之方乖刺如此，則彼智勇材略之人，孰肯抑心下首于宦官、宮妾之門，而陛下之所得以為將帥者，皆庸夫走卒，而猶望其修明軍政，激勸士卒，以強國勢，豈不誤哉！

translations.literal: Generals are the army's fate-arbiter, yet selection and placement is so perverse—then those with wisdom, courage, talent, and strategy, who would willingly suppress their hearts and bow beneath eunuchs' and palace women's gates? Those Your Majesty obtains as generals are all vulgar fellows and runaway soldiers—yet You still hope they will repair military government and rouse soldiers to strengthen the state—is this not error?
translations.idiomatic: Generals hold the army's fate in their hands, yet they are chosen by such corrupt means—what man of wisdom, courage, and talent would bow before eunuchs and palace women? The commanders Your Majesty obtains are vulgar men and common soldiers—yet You still expect them to strengthen the military and the state. Is this not a grave mistake?

sentences.zh: 凡此六事，皆不可緩，而本在於陛下之一心。

translations.literal: All these six matters cannot be delayed, and the root lies in Your Majesty's single heart.
translations.idiomatic: All six of these matters brook no delay, and their root lies in Your Majesty's single heart.

sentences.zh: 一心正則六事無不正，一有人心私欲以介乎其間，則雖欲憊精勞力，以求正夫六事者，亦將徒為文具，而天下之事愈至於不可為矣。

translations.literal: When the one heart is right, the six matters will have nothing not right; if human heart and private desire interpose, then though one exhausts spirit and toils strength to set these six matters right, it will only be empty forms, and affairs under Heaven will the more arrive at impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: When the heart is upright, the six affairs will be upright; but if private desire intrudes, then no amount of labor on those six tasks will be more than empty form, and the empire's affairs will grow ever harder to manage.

sentences.zh: 疏入，夜漏下七刻，上已就寢，亟起秉燭，讀之終篇。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, at the seventh watch after nightfall the emperor had already retired; he hastily rose, lit a candle, and read it to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the night watch had already passed the seventh mark and the emperor had retired; he rose at once, lit a candle, and read it through to the end.

sentences.zh: 明日，除主管太一宮，兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: The next day he was appointed supervisor of the Taiyi Palace, concurrently Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhu Xi was appointed supervisor of the Taiyi Palace and concurrent Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 熹力辭，除秘閣修撰，奉外祠。

translations.literal: Xi forcefully declined; he was appointed Academician of the Secret Repository and granted an outer temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi forcefully declined and was instead appointed Academician of the Secret Repository with an outer temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，再辭職名，仍舊直寶文閣，降詔獎諭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong succeeded, Xi again declined the title but retained Direct Associate in the Hall of Literary Glory; an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong succeeded, Zhu Xi again declined his title but retained his post as Direct Associate in the Hall of Literary Glory; an edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 居數月，除江東轉運副使，以疾辭，改知漳州。

translations.literal: After several months he was appointed Vice Transport Commissioner of Jiangdong; he declined on illness and was changed to prefect of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was appointed Vice Transport Commissioner of Jiangdong; pleading illness, he was instead made prefect of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 奏除屬縣無名之賦七百萬，減經總製錢四百萬。

translations.literal: He memorialized to abolish unauthorized levies of seven million in subordinate counties and reduce comprehensive management funds by four million.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to abolish seven million in unauthorized levies in subordinate counties and cut comprehensive management funds by four million.

sentences.zh: 以習俗未知禮，采古喪葬嫁娶之儀，揭以示之，命父老解說，以教子弟。

translations.literal: Because customs did not yet know ritual, he collected ancient funeral, marriage, and wedding rites, posted them for display, and ordered elders to explain and teach the youth.
translations.idiomatic: Because local customs had not yet learned proper ritual, he gathered ancient rites for funerals, marriages, and weddings, posted them publicly, and had elders explain them to teach the young.

sentences.zh: 土俗崇信釋氏，男女聚僧廬為傅經會，女不嫁者為庵舍以居，熹悉禁之。

translations.literal: Local customs venerated Buddhism; men and women gathered in monastic halls for scripture-recitation assemblies, and women who did not marry lived in nunneries—Xi forbade all this.
translations.idiomatic: The people there revered Buddhism; men and women gathered in monasteries for scripture assemblies, and unmarried women lived in convents—Zhu Xi forbade all of it.

sentences.zh: 常病經界不行之害，會朝論欲行泉、汀、漳三州經界，熹乃訪事宜，擇人物及方量之法上之。

translations.literal: He had long grieved the harm of not implementing land registers; when court discussion wished to implement land registers in Quan, Ting, and Zhang prefectures, Xi inquired into the affairs, selected personnel and measurement methods, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He had long lamented the failure to carry out land registration; when the court proposed implementing it in Quan, Ting, and Zhang prefectures, Zhu Xi investigated the matter, chose personnel and surveying methods, and submitted a plan.

sentences.zh: 而土居豪右侵漁貧弱者以為不便，沮之。

translations.literal: But local powerful gentry who encroached and exploited the poor and weak found it inconvenient and obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: But local magnates who had encroached on the lands of the poor and weak found the plan inconvenient and blocked it.

sentences.zh: 宰相留正，泉人也，其裏黨亦多以為不可行。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Liu Zheng, a native of Quan, and his village associates also mostly thought it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Liu Zheng, a native of Quanzhou, and his local associates also largely declared it unworkable.

sentences.zh: 布衣吳禹圭上書訟其擾人，詔且需後，有旨先行漳州經界。

translations.literal: Commoner Wu Yugui submitted a memorial accusing that it disturbed the people; an edict said to wait for later; there was an order first to implement land registers in Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner, Wu Yugui, memorialized that the project harassed the people; an edict ordered delay, though a directive still called for land registration to proceed first in Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，以子喪請祠。

translations.literal: The next year, on account of a son's death he requested a temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, mourning a son's death, he requested a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 時史浩入見，請收天下人望，乃除熹秘閣修撰，主管南京鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Hao came to audience and requested to gather men of popular esteem; Xi was then appointed Academician of the Secret Repository, supervising the Hongqing Palace in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shi Hao came to audience and urged the court to gather men of public esteem; Zhu Xi was appointed Academician of the Secret Repository, supervising the Hongqing Palace in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 熹再辭，詔：「論撰之職，以寵名儒。」

translations.literal: Xi again declined; an edict said, "The commentary-drafting office is to honor a famed Confucian."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi declined again; an edict declared, "The post of commentator and compiler is meant to honor a renowned scholar."

sentences.zh: 乃拜命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 除荊湖南路轉運副使，辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Transport Commissioner of Jinghu South Circuit and declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Transport Commissioner of Jinghu South Circuit and declined.

sentences.zh: 漳州經界竟報罷，以言不用自劾。

translations.literal: Zhangzhou land registers were ultimately reported cancelled; because his advice was not adopted he impeached himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhangzhou land registration was ultimately reported cancelled; because his advice went unheeded, he submitted a self-impeachment.

sentences.zh: 除知靜江府，辭，主管南京鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Jingjiang Prefecture, declined, and was made supervisor of the Hongqing Palace in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Jingjiang Prefecture, declined, and was assigned to supervise the Hongqing Palace in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，差知潭州，力辭。

translations.literal: Before long he was assigned prefect of Tanzhou and forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was assigned to Tanzhou as prefect and forcefully declined.

sentences.zh: 黃裳為嘉王府詡善，自以學不及熹，乞召為宮僚，王府直講彭龜年亦為大臣言之。

translations.literal: Huang Xiang was Instructor to the Prince of Jia's household; considering his learning did not match Xi's, he requested Xi's summoning as palace staff; the household Direct Lecturer Peng Guinian also spoke of it to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xiang served as Instructor to the Prince of Jia's household; finding his own learning inferior to Zhu Xi's, he asked that Zhu Xi be summoned as a palace official; the household Direct Lecturer Peng Guinian also raised the matter with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 留正曰：「正非不知熹，但其性剛，恐到此不合，反為累耳。」

translations.literal: Liu Zheng said, "It is not that I do not know Xi, but his disposition is firm; I fear that here he will not fit, and instead become a burden."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng said, "It is not that I do not know Zhu Xi, but his temperament is unyielding; I fear he would not fit in here and would instead become a liability."

sentences.zh: 熹方再辭，有旨：「長沙巨屏，得賢為重。」

translations.literal: Xi was just declining again; an order said, "Changsha is a great screen; obtaining the worthy is weighty."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi was declining once more when an edict declared, "Changsha is a great bulwark; securing a worthy man is paramount."

sentences.zh: 遂拜命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 會洞獠擾屬郡，熹遣人諭以禍福，皆降之。

translations.literal: When Cave Yao raided subordinate prefectures, Xi sent men to instruct them on fortune and disaster; all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao tribesmen of the caves raided subordinate prefectures, Zhu Xi sent envoys to instruct them on the consequences of their actions; all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 申敕令，嚴武備，戢奸吏，抑豪民。

translations.literal: He proclaimed edicts, tightened military readiness, restrained corrupt officials, and suppressed powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: He issued edicts, strengthened military preparedness, restrained corrupt officials, and curbed powerful families.

sentences.zh: 所至興學校，明教化，四方學者畢至。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he established schools and clarified instruction; scholars from all directions assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he founded schools and promoted education; scholars came from all quarters.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，趙汝愚首薦熹及陳傅良，有旨赴行在奏事。

translations.literal: When Ningzong took the throne, Zhao Ruyu was first to recommend Xi and Chen Fuliang; an edict ordered them to proceed to the traveling palace and report on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong took the throne, Zhao Ruyu was the first to recommend Zhu Xi and Chen Fuliang; an edict ordered them to proceed to the traveling palace and report on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 熹行且辭，除煥章閣待制、侍講，辭，不許。

translations.literal: Xi was on his way but declined; he was appointed Attendant Gentleman at the Huanzhang Pavilion and Lecture Companion; he declined again and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi was already on his way but declined; he was appointed attendant gentleman at the Huanzhang Pavilion and lecture companion, declined again, and was not permitted to refuse.

sentences.zh: 入對，首言：「乃者，太皇太后躬定大策，陛下寅紹丕圖，可謂處之以權，而庶幾不失其正。

translations.literal: In audience he first said: "Recently the Grand Empress Dowager herself settled the great decision, and Your Majesty reverently inherited the imperial foundation—this may be called handling affairs with expedience while still not losing what is upright.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he first said, "Recently the Grand Empress Dowager herself settled the great decision, and Your Majesty reverently inherited the imperial foundation. This may be called handling affairs with expedience while still not losing what is upright.

sentences.zh: 自頃至今三月矣，或反不能無疑於逆順名實之際，竊為陛下憂之。

translations.literal: From then until now three months have passed, yet some may still harbor doubts at the juncture of legitimacy and nominal reality; I privately worry for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: From then until now three months have passed, yet some may still harbor doubts at the juncture of legitimacy and nominal reality. I worry for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 猶有可諉者，亦曰陛下之心，前日未嘗有求位之計，今日未嘗忘思親之懷，此則所以行權而不失其正之根本也。

translations.literal: There is still something that may be alleged in excuse: it is said that in Your Majesty's heart, you never before harbored a plan to seek the throne, and today you have never forgotten the longing to honor your parent—this is the root by which one may exercise expedience without losing what is upright.
translations.idiomatic: There is still something that may be alleged in excuse: Your Majesty never before harbored a plan to seek the throne, and today has never forgotten the longing to honor your parent. This is the root by which one may exercise expedience without losing what is upright.

sentences.zh: 充未嘗求位之心，以盡負罪引慝之誠，充未嘗忘親之心，以致溫凊定省之禮，而大倫正，大本立矣。」

translations.literal: Fill the heart that never sought the throne, to fulfill the sincerity of accepting guilt and drawing blame upon oneself; fill the heart that never forgets one's parent, to perform the rites of tending comfort and attending in person—and the great human bonds are set right, and the great foundation is established."
translations.idiomatic: Fill the heart that never sought the throne, to fulfill the sincerity of accepting guilt and drawing blame upon oneself; fill the heart that never forgets one's parent, to perform the rites of tending comfort and attending in person—and the great human bonds are set right and the great foundation is established."

sentences.zh: 復面辭待制、侍講，上手劄：「卿經術淵源，正資勸講，次對之職，勿復勞辭，以副朕崇儒重道之意。」

translations.literal: He again declined the Attendant Gentleman and Lecture Companion posts in person; the emperor sent him a handwritten note: "Your classical learning runs deep at its source and is precisely what I need for exhortation in the lecture hall; in the office of waiting remonstrance, do not again trouble yourself with declining, so as to fulfill my purpose of honoring the Ru and valuing the Way."
translations.idiomatic: He again declined the attendant gentleman and lecture companion posts in person. The emperor sent him a handwritten note: "Your classical learning runs deep at its source and is precisely what I need for exhortation in the lecture hall. In the office of waiting remonstrance, do not again trouble yourself with declining, so as to fulfill my purpose of honoring the Ru and valuing the Way."

sentences.zh: 遂拜命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 會趙彥逾按視孝宗山陵，以為土肉淺薄，下有水石。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yanyu inspected Xiaozong's tomb mound, he deemed the covering earth thin and shallow, with water and rocks below.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yanyu inspected Emperor Xiaozong's tomb mound, he judged the covering earth too thin and shallow, with water and rock below.

sentences.zh: 孫逢吉覆按，乞別求吉兆。

translations.literal: Sun Fengji re-inspected and requested separately seeking an auspicious site.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fengji conducted a follow-up inspection and petitioned to seek a new auspicious site.

sentences.zh: 有旨集議，臺史憚之，議中輟。

translations.literal: There was an order to gather for deliberation; the geomancers feared it; the deliberation halted midway.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a collective deliberation, but the geomancers feared the inquiry, and the discussion was suspended midway.

sentences.zh: 熹竟上議狀言：「壽皇聖德，衣冠之藏，當博訪名山，不宜偏信臺史，委之水泉沙礫之中。」

translations.literal: Xi ultimately submitted a deliberation petition, saying, "Emperor Shouhuang's sagely virtue—the burial of his raiment should be sought broadly on famed mountains; one should not one-sidedly trust the geomancers and consign him amid water, springs, sand, and gravel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi ultimately submitted a deliberation memorial stating, "Given Emperor Shouhuang's sagely virtue, his burial garments should be laid to rest after broad inquiry among famed mountains; one must not trust the geomancers alone and consign him to water, springs, sand, and gravel."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: The memorial received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 時論者以為上未還大內，則名體不正而疑議生；

translations.literal: At the time, commentators held that if the Emperor had not yet returned to the Inner Palace, then titles and form would be irregular and suspicions would arise;
translations.idiomatic: Commentators at the time held that if the emperor had not yet returned to the Inner Palace, his title and office would lack proper form and suspicions would arise;

sentences.zh: 金使且來，或有窺伺。

translations.literal: the Jin envoys were about to arrive, and [the Jin] might spy and pry.
translations.idiomatic: Jin envoys were soon expected, and there was fear they might be watching for weakness.

sentences.zh: 有旨修葺舊東宮，為屋三數百間，欲徙居之。

translations.literal: There was an order to repair the old Eastern Palace, making several hundred rooms, with the intention of moving residence there.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the old Eastern Palace renovated into several hundred rooms, with the intention that the emperor would move there.

sentences.zh: 熹奏疏言：

translations.literal: Xi submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi submitted a memorial, stating:

sentences.zh: 此必左右近習倡為此說以誤陛下，而欲因以遂其奸心。

translations.literal: This must surely be close attendants and favored intimates who advocated this talk to mislead Your Majesty, and who wish thereby to carry out their treacherous intent.
translations.idiomatic: This must surely be close attendants and favored intimates who put forward this proposal to mislead Your Majesty, seeking thereby to fulfill their own treacherous designs.

sentences.zh: 臣恐不惟上帝震怒，災異數出，正當恐懼修省之時，不當興此大役，以咈譴告警動之意；

translations.literal: Your servant fears that not only may the Supreme Lord be angered—portents and anomalies appear repeatedly—but that this is precisely a time when one ought to fear and cultivate self-examination; one ought not launch this great labor, so as to rebuff the intent of Heaven's warnings and alarms;
translations.idiomatic: I fear that not only may Heaven be angered—with omens and anomalies appearing one after another—but that this is precisely when Your Majesty should be filled with awe and cultivate self-examination. It is no time to undertake such a great public work, rebuffing the very meaning of Heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 亦恐畿甸百姓饑餓流離、阽於死亡之際，或能怨望忿切，以生他變。

translations.literal: [I] also fear that the common people of the capital region, hungry, starving, displaced, and on the brink of death, may harbor resentment and bitter anger, giving rise to other disturbances.
translations.idiomatic: I also fear that the people of the capital region, starving, displaced, and on the brink of death, may turn to resentment and bitter anger and give rise to other disturbances.

sentences.zh: 不惟無以感格太上皇帝之心，以致未有進見之期，亦恐壽皇在殯，因山未卜，几筵之奉不容少弛，太皇太后、皇太后皆以尊老之年，煢然在憂苦之中，晨昏之養尤不可闕。

translations.literal: Not only would there be no means to move the Retired Emperor's heart, so that there would still be no occasion for an audience; [I] also fear that with Shouhuang lying in state and the mountain tomb not yet chosen, the service at the spirit tablet must not slacken even slightly; the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager, both in their venerable years, are utterly alone in grief and affliction—the morning and evening nursing especially must not be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Not only would this fail to move the Retired Emperor's heart and leave no prospect of an audience, but I also fear that with Emperor Shouhuang still lying in state and his tomb site undetermined, the offerings at the mourning altar must not be relaxed even for a moment. The Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager, both advanced in years, are utterly alone in grief and sorrow; the morning and evening care owed them especially must not be neglected.

sentences.zh: 而四方之人，但見陛下亟欲大治宮室，速得成就，一旦翩然委而去之，以就安便，六軍萬民之心將有扼腕不平者矣。

translations.literal: Yet the people throughout the realm would see only that Your Majesty urgently wished to greatly renovate the palace quarters, to have them quickly completed, and then one day lightly cast them aside and leave, to seek comfort and ease—the hearts of the six armies and the myriad people would surely harbor anguished indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet people throughout the realm would see only that Your Majesty urgently wished to undertake a great renovation of the palace, have it finished at speed, and then one day cast it aside and leave for comfort and ease. The hearts of the armies and the common people would surely fill with anguished indignation.

sentences.zh: 前鑒未遠，甚可懼也。

translations.literal: Recent precedents are not far off; this is greatly to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Recent precedents lie close at hand; this is a matter of grave concern.

sentences.zh: 又聞太上皇后懼忤太上皇帝聖意，不欲其聞太上之稱，又不欲其聞內禪之說，此又慮之過者。

translations.literal: It was also heard that the Retired Empress, fearing to offend the Retired Emperor's sacred intent, did not wish him to hear the title "Retired Emperor," and also did not wish him to hear talk of the abdication—this again was excessive in caution.
translations.idiomatic: It was also reported that the Retired Empress, fearing to offend the Retired Emperor, did not wish him to hear the title "Retired Emperor" or any mention of the abdication—yet this too was excessive caution.

sentences.zh: 殊不知若但如此，而不為宛轉方便，則父子之間，上怨怒而下憂恐，將何時而已。

translations.literal: They did not realize that if matters were handled only in this way, without tactful mediation, then between father and son, with resentment above and fear below, when would it ever end?
translations.idiomatic: They did not realize that if matters were handled only in this way, without tactful mediation, then between father and son—with anger above and fear below—when would it ever end?

sentences.zh: 父子大倫，三綱所系，久而不圖，亦將有借其名以造謗生事者，此又臣之所大懼也。

translations.literal: The great bond between father and son is what the Three Bonds depend upon; if this is not addressed for long, there will also be those who borrow its name to manufacture slander and stir up trouble—this again is what your servant greatly fears.
translations.idiomatic: The bond between father and son is the foundation of the Three Bonds; if this is left unaddressed for long, others will borrow its name to manufacture slander and stir up trouble. This too is what I greatly fear.

sentences.zh: 願陛下明詔大臣，首罷修葺東宮之役，而以其工料回就慈福、重華之間，草創寢殿一二十間，使粗可居。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to issue a clear edict to the great ministers, first abolishing the work of repairing the Eastern Palace, and redirecting its labor and materials back to the halls of Cifu and Chonghua, provisionally building one or two dozen bedchambers so that [the Retired Emperor] may roughly have lodging.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to issue a clear edict to the chief ministers, first halting the renovation of the Eastern Palace and redirecting its labor and materials to the halls of Cifu and Chonghua, provisionally building one or two dozen bedchambers so that the Retired Emperor may have a place to stay.

sentences.zh: 若夫過宮之計，則臣又願陛下下詔自責，減省輿衛，入宮之後，暫變服色，如唐肅宗之改服紫袍、執控馬前者，以伸負罪引慝之誠，則太上皇帝雖有忿怒之情，亦且霍然消散，而歡意浹洽矣。

translations.literal: As for the plan of visiting the palace, your servant further wishes Your Majesty to issue an edict blaming himself, reduce the imperial escort, and after entering the palace temporarily change his dress, as Tang Suzong changed to a purple robe and took the bridle of the horse in front—so as to express the sincerity of bearing guilt and acknowledging fault; then even if the Retired Emperor harbors anger, it would suddenly dissipate, and joy and accord would be complete.
translations.idiomatic: As for the plan of visiting the Retired Emperor's palace, I further urge Your Majesty to issue an edict of self-reproach, reduce the imperial escort, and after entering the palace temporarily change your dress—as Tang Suzong did when he wore a purple robe and took the bridle of the horse before his father—to express sincere remorse and acknowledgment of fault. Then even if the Retired Emperor still harbors anger, it would suddenly dissipate, and joy and reconciliation would follow.

sentences.zh: 至若朝廷之紀綱，則臣又願陛下深詔左右，勿預朝政。

translations.literal: As for the discipline of the court, your servant further wishes Your Majesty to issue a stern edict to those close at hand, that they must not participate in court politics.
translations.idiomatic: As for the discipline of the court, I further urge Your Majesty to issue a stern edict to close attendants forbidding them to intervene in court politics.

sentences.zh: 其實有勳庸而所得褒賞未愜眾論者，亦詔大臣公議其事，稽考令典，厚報其勞。

translations.literal: Those who truly have merit and achievement yet whose rewards and honors do not satisfy public opinion should also be ordered discussed jointly by the great ministers, examined against the established statutes, and richly repaid for their labor.
translations.idiomatic: Those who truly have rendered meritorious service yet whose rewards do not satisfy public opinion should also be ordered discussed jointly by the chief ministers, examined against established statutes, and richly repaid for their labors.

sentences.zh: 而凡號令之弛張，人才之進退，則一委之二三大臣，使之反覆較量，勿循己見，酌取公論，奏而行之。

translations.literal: And as for the tightening and loosening of orders and the advancement and dismissal of talent, let all be entrusted to two or three great ministers, causing them to weigh matters repeatedly, not follow their own views, take public opinion into account, and submit [recommendations] for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: As for the tightening and loosening of government orders and the advancement and dismissal of talent, all should be entrusted to two or three chief ministers, who should weigh matters repeatedly, not follow their own views alone, take public opinion into account, and submit recommendations for implementation.

sentences.zh: 有不當者，繳駁論難，擇其善者稱制臨決，則不惟近習不得干預朝權，大臣不得專任己私，而陛下亦得以益明習天下之事，而無所疑於得失之算矣。

translations.literal: Where there is what is improper, [memorials should be] returned with objections and debated; choose what is good and decide by imperial command—then not only will close intimates be unable to intervene in court power, and great ministers unable to monopolize their private interests, but Your Majesty also will increasingly become versed in affairs throughout the realm, and have no doubts in calculating gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Where a proposal is improper, memorials should be returned with objections and debated; choose what is best and decide by imperial command. Then not only will close intimates be unable to intervene in court power and great ministers unable to monopolize their private interests, but Your Majesty will also grow increasingly versed in affairs throughout the realm and have no doubts in weighing gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 若夫山陵之卜，則願黜台史之說，別求草澤，以營新宮，使壽皇之遺體得安於內，而宗社生靈皆蒙福於外矣。

translations.literal: As for the selection of the mountain tomb, [I] wish to dismiss the geomancers' proposal, separately seek [a site] among the wilds and marshes, and build a new mausoleum, so that Shouhuang's remains may rest peacefully within, and the altars of state and the living may all receive blessing without.
translations.idiomatic: As for the selection of the tomb site, I urge dismissal of the geomancers' proposal and a separate search among remote hills and marshes for a new mausoleum, so that Emperor Shouhuang's remains may rest in peace within and the altars of state and the people may all receive blessing without.

sentences.zh: 疏入不報，然上亦未有怒熹意也。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no response; yet the Emperor also had no intent to be angry at Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and went unanswered, yet the emperor showed no anger toward Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 每以所講編次成帙以進，上亦開懷容納。

translations.literal: [He] regularly compiled his lectures into fascicles and submitted them; the Emperor also received them with open heart and acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly compiled his lecture materials into volumes and presented them to the throne; the emperor received them openly and with acceptance.

sentences.zh: 熹又奏勉上進德云：「願陛下日用之間，以求放心為之本，而於玩經觀史，親近儒學，益用力焉。

translations.literal: Xi again submitted a memorial urging the Emperor to advance in virtue, saying: "I wish Your Majesty, in your daily conduct, to take seeking a tranquil mind as the foundation, and in reading the classics and observing history, drawing near to Confucian learning, to exert yourself all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi again submitted a memorial urging the emperor to advance in virtue, stating: "I urge Your Majesty, in your daily conduct, to take restoring a tranquil mind as the foundation, and in reading the classics, studying history, and drawing near to Confucian learning, to exert yourself all the more.

sentences.zh: 數召大臣，切劘治道，群臣進對，亦賜溫顏，反覆詢訪，以求政事之得失，民情之休戚，而又因以察其人才之邪正短長，庶於天下之事各得其理。」

translations.literal: Frequently summon the great ministers and sharply examine the way of governance; when the multitude of officials advance to respond, also grant them a warm countenance, repeatedly inquire and consult, so as to seek the gains and losses of government affairs and the weal and woe of the people's sentiments—and thereby also observe the crookedness and straightness, the strengths and weaknesses of their talent—so that affairs throughout the realm may each obtain their proper principle."
translations.idiomatic: Frequently summon the chief ministers and sharply examine the way of governance; when officials come forward to respond, grant them a warm countenance and repeatedly inquire and consult, so as to learn the gains and losses of government affairs and the weal and woe of the people—and thereby also observe the integrity, ability, and character of their talent—so that affairs throughout the realm may each be handled according to principle."

sentences.zh: 熹奏：「禮經敕令，子為父，嫡孫承重為祖父，皆斬衰三年；

translations.literal: Xi submitted: "The ritual classics and imperial commands [state that] a son [mourning] for a father, and an eldest grandson bearing the chief mourning for a grandfather, both [observe] zhan mourning for three years;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi submitted: "The ritual classics and imperial commands state that a son mourning for a father, and an eldest grandson bearing the chief mourning for a grandfather, both observe the deepest mourning for three years;

sentences.zh: 嫡子當為其父後，不能襲位執喪，則嫡孫繼統而代之執喪。

translations.literal: the eldest son ought to succeed his father, [but] if he cannot inherit the position and observe mourning, then the eldest grandson succeeds to the line and performs mourning in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son ought to succeed his father; if he cannot inherit the position and observe mourning, then the eldest grandson succeeds to the line and performs mourning in his stead.

sentences.zh: 自漢文短喪，歷代因之，天子遂無三年之喪。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Wen of Han shortened mourning, successive generations followed this, and the Son of Heaven thus had no three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Wen of Han shortened the mourning period, successive generations followed his example, and the Son of Heaven thus ceased to observe three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 為父且然，則嫡孫承重可知。

translations.literal: If this is so even for [mourning] a father, then [mourning as] an eldest grandson bearing the chief mourning can be understood.
translations.idiomatic: If this is so even for mourning a father, then the case of an eldest grandson bearing the chief mourning can readily be understood.

sentences.zh: 人紀廢壞，三綱不明，千有餘年，莫能厘正。

translations.literal: Human norms were ruined and destroyed, the Three Bonds unclear—for more than a thousand years none could rectify this.
translations.idiomatic: Human norms were ruined, the Three Bonds left unclear—for more than a thousand years no one could rectify this.

sentences.zh: 壽皇聖帝至性自天，易月之外，猶執通喪，朝衣朝冠皆用大布，所宜著在方冊，為萬世法程。

translations.literal: The Sagely Emperor Shouhuang's utmost nature came from Heaven; beyond the change of garments at one month, he still observed full mourning, and for court dress and court cap all used coarse cloth—this ought to be recorded in the official registers as a model for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shouhuang's utmost filial nature came from Heaven; beyond the change of garments at one month, he still observed full mourning, wearing coarse cloth for court dress and court cap. This ought to be recorded in the official registers as a model for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 間者，遺誥初頒，太上皇帝偶違康豫，不能躬就喪次。

translations.literal: Recently, when the testamentary edict was first promulgated, the Retired Emperor happened to be unwell and could not personally attend the mourning place.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when the testamentary edict was first promulgated, the Retired Emperor happened to be unwell and could not personally attend the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 陛下以世嫡承大統，則承重之服著在禮律，所宜遵壽皇已行之法。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, as the legitimate heir of the age succeeding to the great succession, ought to wear the mourning of bearing the chief mourning as set forth in ritual law, and ought to follow the practice already carried out by Shouhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, as the legitimate heir succeeding to the great succession, ought to wear the mourning of bearing the chief mourning as set forth in ritual law and follow the practice already carried out by Emperor Shouhuang.

sentences.zh: 一時倉卒，不及詳議，遂用漆紗淺黃之服，不惟上違禮律，且使壽皇已行之禮舉而復墜，臣竊痛之。

translations.literal: For a time, in haste, there was no opportunity for detailed deliberation, and lacquered gauze in pale yellow was used—this not only violated ritual law above, but also caused the rites already practiced by Shouhuang to be raised up only to fall again; your servant privately grieves at this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, in haste, there was no opportunity for detailed deliberation, and lacquered gauze in pale yellow was used. This not only violated ritual law but also caused the rites already practiced by Emperor Shouhuang to be raised up only to fall again. I grieve at this in private.

sentences.zh: 然既往之失不及追改，唯有將來啟殯發引，禮當復用初喪之服。」

translations.literal: Yet past errors cannot be pursued and changed; only for the future, when the coffin is opened and the funeral procession departs, the rites ought to restore the garments of initial mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Yet past errors cannot be pursued and changed; only for the future, when the coffin is opened and the funeral procession departs, the rites ought to restore the garments of initial mourning."

sentences.zh: 會孝宗祔廟，議宗廟迭毀之制，孫逢吉、曾三復首請並祧僖、宣二祖，奉太祖居第一室，祫祭則正東向之位。

translations.literal: It happened that when Emperor Xiaozong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, the system of successive removal in the temple was debated; Sun Fengji and Zeng Sanfu first requested jointly removing Emperor Xi and Emperor Xuan from the main line, placing Emperor Taizu in the first chamber, and at the joint sacrifice placing him in the due east-facing position.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, the system of successive removal in the temple was debated. Sun Fengji and Zeng Sanfu first requested jointly removing Emperors Xi and Xuan from the main line, placing Emperor Taizu in the first chamber, and at the joint sacrifice placing him in the due east-facing position.

sentences.zh: 有旨集議：僖、順、翼、宣四祖祧主，宜有所歸。

translations.literal: There was an order to gather for deliberation: the removed spirit tablets of the four ancestors Xi, Shun, Yi, and Xuan ought to have a place to which they return.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a collective deliberation: the removed spirit tablets of the four ancestors Xi, Shun, Yi, and Xuan ought to have a proper place of enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 自太祖皇帝首尊四祖之廟，治平間，議者以世數浸遠，請遷僖祖於夾室。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Taizu first honored the temples of the four ancestors, during the Zhiping era commentators, because generations had grown distant, requested moving Emperor Xi to a side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Taizu first honored the temples of the four ancestors, during the Zhiping era commentators, because generations had grown distant, requested moving Emperor Xi to a side chamber.

sentences.zh: 後王安石等奏，僖祖有廟，與稷、契無異，請復其舊。

translations.literal: Later Wang Anshi and others memorialized that Emperor Xi had a temple, no different from Hou Ji and Qi, and requested restoring the former arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Anshi and others memorialized that Emperor Xi had a temple, no different from Hou Ji and Qi, and requested restoring the former arrangement.

sentences.zh: 時相趙汝愚雅不以復祀僖祖為然，侍從多從其說。

translations.literal: At the time, Chief Councillor Zhao Ruyu by nature did not approve of restoring sacrifice to Emperor Xi; most of the attendant officials followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Chief Councillor Zhao Ruyu by nature did not approve of restoring sacrifice to Emperor Xi; most of the attendant officials followed his view.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書鄭僑欲且祧宣祖而祔孝宗。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zheng Qiao wished temporarily to remove Emperor Xuan and enshrine Emperor Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zheng Qiao wished temporarily to remove Emperor Xuan and enshrine Emperor Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 熹以為藏之夾室，則是以祖宗之主下藏於子孫之夾室，神宗復奉以為始祖，已為得禮之正，而合于人心，所謂有舉之而莫敢廢者乎。

translations.literal: Xi held that storing [the tablets] in a side chamber meant placing the spirit tablets of the ancestors and forebears down in the side chamber of their descendants; when Emperor Shenzong again honored [Emperor Xi] as founding ancestor, this already obtained the correctness of ritual and accorded with the hearts of the people—is this not what is called "once it was raised up, none dared abolish it"?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi held that storing the tablets in a side chamber meant placing the spirit tablets of the ancestors down in the side chamber of their descendants. When Emperor Shenzong again honored Emperor Xi as founding ancestor, this already accorded with proper ritual and with the hearts of the people—is this not what is meant by "once it was raised up, none dared abolish it"?

sentences.zh: 又擬為《廟制》以辨，以為物豈有無本而生者。

translations.literal: He also drafted a "Temple System" to clarify [the matter], holding that nothing can be born without a root.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted a "Temple System" to clarify the matter, holding that nothing can be born without a root.

sentences.zh: 廟堂不以聞，即毀撤僖、宣廟室，更創別廟以奉四祖。

translations.literal: The temple authorities did not report [his views]; they immediately demolished the temple chambers of Emperors Xi and Xuan and newly built separate temples to honor the four ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The temple authorities did not report his views; they immediately demolished the temple chambers of Emperors Xi and Xuan and newly built separate temples to honor the four ancestors.

sentences.zh: 始，甯宗之立，韓侂胄自謂有定策功，居中用事。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Ningzong was established [as heir], Han Tuozhou considered himself to have merit in fixing the succession and held power at court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when Ningzong was established as heir, Han Tuozhou considered himself to have merit in fixing the succession and held power at court.

sentences.zh: 熹憂其害政，數以為言，且約吏部侍郎彭龜年共論之。

translations.literal: Xi worried that he would harm governance, repeatedly spoke of this, and also arranged with Vice Minister of Personnel Peng Guinian to discuss it together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi worried that he would harm governance, spoke of this repeatedly, and also arranged with Vice Minister of Personnel Peng Guinian to discuss the matter together.

sentences.zh: 會龜年出護使客，熹乃上疏斥言左右竊柄之失，在講筵復申言之。

translations.literal: It happened that Guinian went out to serve as commissioner for receiving envoys; Xi then submitted a memorial denouncing the fault of those close at hand usurping power, and again stated this at the lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Guinian went out to serve as commissioner for receiving envoys, Zhu Xi submitted a memorial denouncing the fault of close attendants usurping power and again stated this at the lecture hall.

sentences.zh: 御批云：「憫卿耆艾，恐難立講，已除卿宮觀。」

translations.literal: An imperial annotation read: "Taking pity on your age and venerability, fearing difficulty in lecturing standing, [We] have already appointed you to a temple commission post."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial annotation read: "Taking pity on your age and venerability, fearing difficulty in lecturing while standing, We have already appointed you to a temple commission post."

sentences.zh: 汝愚袖御筆還上，且諫且拜。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu tucked the imperial brush [writing] and returned it upward, remonstrating while bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu tucked the emperor's handwritten note into his sleeve and returned it to the throne, remonstrating while bowing.

sentences.zh: 內侍王德謙徑以御筆付熹，台諫爭留，不可。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Wang Deqian directly handed the imperial brush [writing] to Xi; the censorate remonstrators struggled to retain [him]—it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Wang Deqian directly handed the emperor's note to Zhu Xi; censorate remonstrators struggled to retain him, but could not.

sentences.zh: 樓鑰、陳傅良旋封還錄黃，修注官劉光祖、鄧馹封章交上。

translations.literal: Lou Yue and Chen Fuliang immediately sealed and returned the recorded draft in yellow; the revising annotators Liu Guangzu and Deng Yi submitted sealed memorials in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Yue and Chen Fuliang immediately sealed and returned the recorded draft; the revising annotators Liu Guangzu and Deng Yi submitted sealed memorials in succession.

sentences.zh: 熹行，被命除寶文閣待制，與州郡差遣，辭。

translations.literal: Xi departed; he was ordered appointed as Hanlin Academician of the Baowen Pavilion, with assignment to a prefecture or circuit—he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi departed; he was ordered appointed as Hanlin Academician of the Baowen Pavilion with assignment to a prefecture or circuit, but declined.

sentences.zh: 尋除知江陵府，辭，仍乞追還新舊職名，詔依舊煥章閣待制，提舉南京鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Jiangling—he declined, and still requested the return of both old and new titles and offices; an edict ordered him to remain as before Hanlin Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion, with charge of the Hongqing Palace in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Jiangling; he declined and still requested the return of both old and new titles and offices. An edict ordered him to remain as Hanlin Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion, with charge of the Hongqing Palace in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 慶元元年初，趙汝愚既相，收召四方知名之士，中外引領望治，熹獨惕然以侂胄用事為慮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the first year of Qingyuan, after Zhao Ruyu had become chief councillor, he gathered and recalled renowned men from throughout the realm; within and without the court all stretched their necks hoping for good governance—Xi alone was apprehensive, taking Tuozhou's wielding of power as a concern.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the first year of Qingyuan, after Zhao Ruyu had become chief councillor, he gathered and recalled renowned men from throughout the realm; within and without the court all looked on hoping for good governance. Zhu Xi alone was apprehensive, taking Han Tuozhou's wielding of power as a concern.

sentences.zh: 既屢為上言，以數以手書啟汝愚，當用厚賞酬其勞，勿使得預朝政，有「防微杜漸，謹不可忽」之語。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly spoken to the Emperor on this, he also repeatedly by handwritten letter apprised Ruyu that he ought to use rich rewards to repay [Tuozhou's] labor, and must not allow him to participate in court politics—there were the words "guard against the subtle and stop the gradual; this must not be neglected."
translations.idiomatic: Having repeatedly spoken to the emperor on this, he also repeatedly by handwritten letter apprised Zhao Ruyu that he ought to use rich rewards to repay Han Tuozhou's labors and must not allow him to participate in court politics—writing, "Guard against the subtle and stop the gradual; this must not be neglected."

sentences.zh: 汝愚方謂其易制，不以為意。

translations.literal: Ruyu just then considered him easy to control and did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu just then considered him easy to control and did not take it to heart.

sentences.zh: 及是，汝愚亦以誣逐，而朝廷大權悉歸侂胄矣。

translations.literal: By this time, Ruyu also was driven out on false charges, and great power at court all returned to Tuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: By this time, Zhao Ruyu also was driven out on false charges, and great power at court all returned to Han Tuozhou.

sentences.zh: 熹始以廟議自劾，不許，以疾再乞休致，詔：「辭職謝事，非朕優賢之意，依舊秘閣修撰。」

translations.literal: Xi first submitted a self-impeachment over the temple deliberation—it was not accepted; citing illness he again requested retirement; an edict read: "Resigning office and declining affairs is not Our intent in honoring the worthy; [he is ordered to remain] as before Secretary of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi first submitted a self-impeachment over the temple deliberation—it was not accepted. Citing illness, he again requested retirement. An edict read: "Resigning office and declining affairs is not Our intent in honoring the worthy; he is ordered to remain as Secretary of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 二年，沈繼祖為監察御史，誣熹十罪，詔落職罷祠，門人蔡元定亦送道州編管。

translations.literal: In the second year, Shen Jizu as Investigating Censor falsely charged Xi with ten crimes; an edict stripped him of office and abolished his temple stipend; his disciple Cai Yuanding was also sent to Daozhou for supervised residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Shen Jizu as Investigating Censor falsely charged Zhu Xi with ten crimes. An edict stripped him of office and abolished his temple stipend; his disciple Cai Yuanding was also sent to Daozhou for supervised residence.

sentences.zh: 四年，熹以年近七十，申乞致仕，五年，依所請。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Xi, because his age was nearly seventy, submitted a request for retirement; in the fifth year, [the request] was granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Zhu Xi, because his age was nearly seventy, submitted a request for retirement; in the fifth year, the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died, aged seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 疾且革，手書屬其子在及門人范念德、黃幹，拳拳以勉學及修正遺書為言。

translations.literal: When his illness was nearly critical, he by hand wrote instructions to his son Zai and his disciples Fan Niande and Huang Gan, earnestly speaking of encouraging learning and correcting and completing his remaining writings.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness was nearly critical, he wrote by hand instructions to his son Zhu Zai and his disciples Fan Niande and Huang Gan, earnestly urging them to encourage learning and to correct and complete his remaining writings.

sentences.zh: 翌日，正坐整衣冠，就枕而逝。

translations.literal: The next day, sitting upright, he straightened his cap and robes, lay down on his pillow, and passed away.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, sitting upright, he straightened his cap and robes, lay down on his pillow, and passed away.

sentences.zh: 熹登第五十年，仕於外者僅九考，立朝才四十日。

translations.literal: From Xi's passing the examinations for fifty years, he served outside [the capital] for only nine evaluations, and stood at court for only forty days.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhu Xi's passing the examinations for fifty years, he served outside the capital for only nine terms of evaluation and stood at court for only forty days.

sentences.zh: 家故貧，少依父友劉子羽，寓建之崇安，後徙建陽之考亭，簞瓢屢空，晏如也。

translations.literal: His family was originally poor; in youth he relied on his father's friend Liu Ziyu, lodging in Chong'an in Jian, later moving to Kaoting in Jianyang; the basket and gourd were often empty, yet he was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: His family was originally poor; in youth he relied on his father's friend Liu Ziyu, lodging in Chong'an in Jian Prefecture, later moving to Kaoting in Jianyang. The basket and gourd were often empty, yet he was at ease.

sentences.zh: 諸生之自遠而至者，豆飯藜羹，率與之共。

translations.literal: Students who came from afar—all ate bean rice and wild vegetable soup, and he generally shared with them.
translations.idiomatic: Students who came from afar all ate bean rice and wild vegetable soup, and he generally shared meals with them.

sentences.zh: 往往稱貸於人以給用，而非其道義則一介不取也。

translations.literal: He often borrowed from others to supply his needs, yet if it was not in accord with the Way and righteousness, not one cash would he take.
translations.idiomatic: He often borrowed from others to supply his needs, yet if something was not in accord with the Way and righteousness, not one cash would he take.

sentences.zh: 自熹去國，侂胄勢益張。

translations.literal: From the time Xi left the court, Tuozhou's power grew ever more expansive.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Zhu Xi left the court, Han Tuozhou's power grew ever more expansive.

sentences.zh: 何澹為中司，首論專門之學，文詐沽名，乞辨真偽。

translations.literal: He Dan as Chief of the Censorate Bureau first denounced specialized learning, literary deception and trading on reputation, and requested distinguishing true from false.
translations.idiomatic: He Dan as Chief of the Censorate Bureau first denounced specialized learning as literary deception and trading on reputation, and requested distinguishing true from false.

sentences.zh: 劉德秀仕長沙，不為張栻之徒所禮，及為諫官，首論留正引偽學之罪。

translations.literal: Liu Dexiu served in Changsha and was not treated with courtesy by Zhang Shi's followers; when he became remonstrating official, he first denounced Liu Zheng for the crime of promoting false learning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dexiu served in Changsha and was not treated with courtesy by Zhang Shi's followers. When he became a remonstrating official, he first denounced Liu Zheng for the crime of promoting false learning.

sentences.zh: 「偽學」之稱，蓋自此始。

translations.literal: The designation "false learning" began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The designation "false learning" began from this.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿胡紘言：「比年偽學猖獗，圖為不軌，望宣諭大臣，權住進擬。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Hu Hong stated: "In recent years false learning has run rampant, plotting irregular conduct; [I] hope [Your Majesty] will proclaim and instruct the great ministers temporarily to halt nominations for appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Hu Hong stated: "In recent years false learning has run rampant, plotting irregular conduct. I hope Your Majesty will proclaim and instruct the chief ministers temporarily to halt nominations for appointment."

sentences.zh: 遂召陳賈為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Chen Jia was then summoned as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jia was then summoned as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 未幾，熹有奪職之命。

translations.literal: Before long, Xi received an order stripping him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Zhu Xi received an order stripping him of office.

sentences.zh: 劉三傑以前御史論熹、汝愚、劉光祖、徐誼之徒，前日之偽黨，至此又變而為逆黨。

translations.literal: Liu Sanjie, formerly an investigating censor, denounced Xi, Ruyu, Liu Guangzu, Xu Yi, and their kind—the false faction of former days—who by this time had again changed into a rebellious faction.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sanjie, formerly an investigating censor, denounced Zhu Xi, Zhao Ruyu, Liu Guangzu, Xu Yi, and their kind—the false faction of former days—who by this time had again been recast as a rebellious faction.

sentences.zh: 即日除三傑右正言。

translations.literal: That same day Sanjie was appointed Right Rectifier of Discourse.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Liu Sanjie was appointed Right Rectifier of Discourse.

sentences.zh: 右諫議大夫姚愈論道學權臣結為死黨，窺伺神器。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrating Grandee Yao Yu denounced the Learning of the Way faction and powerful ministers forming a sworn faction, spying on the sacred regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrating Grandee Yao Yu denounced the Learning of the Way faction and powerful ministers forming a sworn faction and spying on the sacred regalia.

sentences.zh: 乃命直學士院高文虎草詔諭天下，於是攻偽日急，選人餘嘉至上書乞斬熹。

translations.literal: An order was then issued to Academician of the Direct Academy Gao Wenhu to draft an edict proclaiming this to the realm; thereafter attacks on the false grew daily urgent, and the candidate Yu Jiazhi submitted a memorial requesting that Xi be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: An order was then issued to Academician of the Direct Academy Gao Wenhu to draft an edict proclaiming this to the realm. Thereafter attacks on the false grew daily urgent, and the candidate Yu Jiazhi submitted a memorial requesting that Zhu Xi be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 方是時，士之繩趨尺步、稍以儒名者，無所容其身。

translations.literal: At that time, scholars who walked to the measure of the cord and foot-rule and were even slightly known by Confucian reputation had no place to contain their persons.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, scholars who walked to the measure of the cord and foot-rule and were even slightly known by Confucian reputation had no place to stand.

sentences.zh: 從遊之士，特立不顧者，屏伏丘壑；

translations.literal: Among those who had studied with [him], those who stood firm and paid no heed hid themselves in hills and ravines;
translations.idiomatic: Among those who had studied with him, those who stood firm and paid no heed hid themselves in hills and ravines;

sentences.zh: 依阿巽懦者，更名他師，過門不入，甚至變易衣冠，狎遊市肆，以自別其非黨。

translations.literal: those who fawned and were weak changed their teachers' names, passed his gate without entering, and even changed their dress, idly roaming marketplaces, so as to distinguish themselves as not of the faction.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fawned and were weak changed their teachers' names, passed his gate without entering, and even changed their dress and idly roamed marketplaces so as to distinguish themselves as not of the faction.

sentences.zh: 而熹日與諸生講學不休，或勸以謝遣生徒者，笑而不答。

translations.literal: Yet Xi daily lectured with his students without ceasing; when some advised him to dismiss his disciples, he smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhu Xi daily lectured with his students without ceasing; when some advised him to dismiss his disciples, he smiled and did not answer.

sentences.zh: 有籍田令陳景思者，故相康伯之孫也，與侂胄有姻連，勸侂胄勿為已甚，侂胄意亦漸悔。

translations.literal: There was the Field-Allotment Magistrate Chen Jingsi, grandson of the former chief councillor Kangbo, connected to Tuozhou by marriage; he advised Tuozhou not to go too far, and Tuozhou's mind also gradually came to regret.
translations.idiomatic: There was the Field-Allotment Magistrate Chen Jingsi, grandson of the former chief councillor Chen Kangbo, connected to Han Tuozhou by marriage. He advised Han Tuozhou not to go too far, and Han Tuozhou's mind also gradually came to regret.

sentences.zh: 熹既沒，將葬，言者謂：四方偽徒期會，送偽師之葬，會聚之間，非妄談時人短長，則繆議時政得失，望令守臣約束。

translations.literal: After Xi had died and was about to be buried, remonstrators stated: "False followers from the four directions will assemble by appointment to escort the false teacher's burial; in their gatherings, if they are not recklessly discussing the faults and merits of men of the time, they will be absurdly debating the gains and losses of current government—[I] hope [Your Majesty] will order guarding officials to restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Xi had died and was about to be buried, remonstrators stated: "False followers from the four directions will assemble by appointment to escort the false teacher's burial. In their gatherings, if they are not recklessly discussing the faults and merits of men of the time, they will be absurdly debating the gains and losses of current government. I hope Your Majesty will order local officials to restrain them.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The request] was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰初，學禁稍弛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiatai, the proscription on learning was slightly relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiatai era, the proscription on learning was slightly relaxed.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔：「朱熹已致仕，除華文閣待制，與致仕恩澤。」

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict read: "Zhu Xi has already retired; [he is appointed] Hanlin Academician of the Huawen Pavilion, with retirement honors."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, an edict read: "Zhu Xi has already retired; he is appointed Hanlin Academician of the Huawen Pavilion, with retirement honors."

sentences.zh: 後侂胄死，詔賜熹遺表恩澤，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Later, after Tuozhou died, an edict granted the honors of Xi's final memorial; his posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Han Tuozhou died, an edict granted the honors of Zhu Xi's final memorial; his posthumous title was Wen.

sentences.zh: 尋贈中大夫，特贈寶謨閣直學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was posthumously promoted to Grandee of the Palace, and specially posthumously promoted to Academician of the Baomo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posthumously promoted to Grandee of the Palace and specially posthumously promoted to Academician of the Baomo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 理宗寶慶三年，贈太師，追封信國公，改徽國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoqing under Emperor Lizong, he was posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xin, [then] changed to Duke of Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoqing under Emperor Lizong, he was posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xin, then changed to Duke of Hui.

sentences.zh: 始，熹少時，慨然有求道之志。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Xi was young, he was stirred and had the aspiration of seeking the Way.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when Zhu Xi was young, he was stirred and had the aspiration of seeking the Way.

sentences.zh: 父松病亟，嘗屬熹曰：「籍溪胡原仲、白水劉致中、屏山劉彥沖三人，學有淵源，吾所敬畏，吾即死，汝往事之，而惟其言之聽。」

translations.literal: When his father Song's illness was critical, he once instructed Xi, saying: "Jixi Hu Yuanzhong, Baishui Liu Zhizhong, and Pingshan Liu Yanchong—the three men's learning has deep sources; they are those I revere; when I die, you should go and serve them, and listen only to their words."
translations.idiomatic: When his father Zhu Song's illness was critical, he once instructed Zhu Xi, saying: "Jixi Hu Yuanzhong, Baishui Liu Zhizhong, and Pingshan Liu Yanchong—the three men's learning has deep sources; they are those I revere. When I die, you should go and serve them, and listen only to their words."

sentences.zh: 三人，謂胡憲、劉勉之、劉子翬也。

translations.literal: The three men were Hu Xian, Liu Mianzhi, and Liu Zihui.
translations.idiomatic: The three men were Hu Xian, Liu Mianzhi, and Liu Zihui.

sentences.zh: 故熹之學既博求之經傳，復遍交當世有識之士。

translations.literal: Therefore Xi's learning both broadly sought [understanding] in the classics and commentaries, and also widely associated with knowledgeable men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zhu Xi's learning both broadly sought understanding in the classics and commentaries and also widely associated with knowledgeable men of the age.

sentences.zh: 延平李侗老矣，嘗學于羅從彥，熹歸自同安，不遠數百里，徒步往從之。

translations.literal: Yanping Li Tong was already old; he had once studied under Luo Congyan; when Xi returned from Tong'an, [he went] not less than several hundred li, walking on foot to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong of Yanping was already old; he had once studied under Luo Congyan. When Zhu Xi returned from Tong'an, he traveled not less than several hundred li on foot to follow him.

sentences.zh: 其為學，大抵窮理以致其知，反躬以踐其實，而以居敬為主。

translations.literal: His pursuit of learning, broadly speaking, was to exhaust principle to extend knowledge, turn inward to practice what is real, and take reverent composure as the main thing.
translations.idiomatic: His pursuit of learning, broadly speaking, was to exhaust principle to extend knowledge, turn inward to practice what is real, and take reverent composure as the main thing.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂聖賢道統之傳散在方冊，聖經之旨不明，而道統之傳始晦。

translations.literal: He once said that the transmission of the sages' Way was scattered in records, the intent of the sacred classics was unclear, and the transmission of the Way therefore began to grow obscure.
translations.idiomatic: He once said that the transmission of the sages' Way was scattered in records, the intent of the sacred classics was unclear, and the transmission of the Way therefore began to grow obscure.

sentences.zh: 於是竭其精力，以研窮聖賢之經訓。

translations.literal: Thereupon he exhausted his energy and strength to investigate thoroughly the sages' classic exegeses.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he exhausted his energy and strength to investigate thoroughly the sages' classic exegeses.

sentences.zh: 所著書有：《易》本義、啟蒙、《蓍卦考誤》，《詩集傳》，《大學中庸》章句、或問、《論語》、《孟子》集注、《太極圖》、《通書》、《西銘解》、《楚辭》集注、辨證，《韓文考異》；

translations.literal: Books he authored include: Original Meaning of the Changes, Enlightenment, Examination of Errors in Divination by Yarrow Stalks, Collected Commentary on the Odes, Chapter and Sentence [commentaries] on the Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean, Questions [on those texts], Collected Commentaries on the Analects and Mencius, Explications of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Penetrating the Classic, and Western Inscription, Collected Commentary and Evidential Analysis on the Songs of Chu, and Examination of Variants in Han Yu's Writings;
translations.idiomatic: Books he authored include: Original Meaning of the Changes, Enlightenment, Examination of Errors in Divination by Yarrow Stalks, Collected Commentary on the Odes, Chapter and Sentence commentaries on the Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean, Questions on those texts, Collected Commentaries on the Analects and Mencius, Explications of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Penetrating the Classic, and Western Inscription, Collected Commentary and Evidential Analysis on the Songs of Chu, and Examination of Variants in Han Yu's Writings;

sentences.zh: 所編次有：《論孟集議》，《孟子指要》，《中庸輯略》，《孝經刊誤》，《小學書》，《通鑒綱目》，《宋名臣言行錄》，《家禮》，《近思錄》，《河南程氏遺書》，《伊洛淵源錄》，皆行於世。

translations.literal: Works he compiled and arranged include: Collected Deliberations on the Analects and Mencius, Essential Points of Mencius, Abridged Doctrine of the Mean, Corrections to the Classic of Filial Piety, Elementary Learning, Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror, Records of Words and Deeds of Famous Song Ministers, Family Rituals, Reflections on Things at Hand, Surviving Writings of the Cheng Family of Henan, and Record of the Origins of the Yi-Luo [School]—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Works he compiled and arranged include: Collected Deliberations on the Analects and Mencius, Essential Points of Mencius, Abridged Doctrine of the Mean, Corrections to the Classic of Filial Piety, Elementary Learning, Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror, Records of Words and Deeds of Famous Song Ministers, Family Rituals, Reflections on Things at Hand, Surviving Writings of the Cheng Family of Henan, and Record of the Origins of the Yi-Luo School—all circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 熹沒，朝廷以其《大學》、《語》、《孟》、《中庸》訓說立於學官。

translations.literal: When Xi died, the court established his expository commentaries on the Great Learning, Analects, Mencius, and Doctrine of the Mean at the official schools.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Xi's death, the court placed his commentaries on the Great Learning, Analects, Mencius, and Doctrine of the Mean in the official curriculum.

sentences.zh: 又有《儀禮經傳通解》未脫稿，亦在學官。

translations.literal: There was also his Ceremonial Rites General Explication of Classic and Commentaries, unfinished at his death, which likewise entered the official schools.
translations.idiomatic: His Ceremonial Rites General Explication of Classic and Commentaries, still incomplete at his death, was also adopted for the official schools.

sentences.zh: 平生為文凡一百卷，生徒問答凡八十卷，別錄十卷。

translations.literal: In his lifetime he wrote one hundred juan of essays, eighty juan of student questions and answers, and ten juan of separate records.
translations.idiomatic: Over his lifetime he produced one hundred juan of prose, eighty juan of exchanges with disciples, and ten juan of miscellaneous records.

sentences.zh: 理宗紹定末，秘書郎李心傳乞以司馬光、周敦頤、邵雍、張載、程顥、程頤、朱熹七人列於從祀，不報。

translations.literal: At the end of the Shaoding reign of Emperor Lizong, Secretariat Attendant Li Xinchuan petitioned that Sima Guang, Zhou Dunyi, Shao Yong, Zhang Zai, Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, and Zhu Xi be added as collateral sacrifices; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Shaoding era, Secretariat Attendant Li Xinchuan asked that Sima Guang, Zhou Dunyi, Shao Yong, Zhang Zai, Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, and Zhu Xi be enshrined as collateral sacrifices in the Confucian temple; the petition went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年正月，上視學，手詔以周、張、二程及熹從祀孔子廟。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Chunyou, the Emperor inspected the schools and issued a personal edict adding Zhou, Zhang, the two Chengs, and Xi as collateral sacrifices in the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chunyou 1, the emperor visited the schools and by personal edict added Zhou Dunyi, Zhang Zai, the two Chengs, and Zhu Xi to the collateral sacrifices in Confucius's temple.

sentences.zh: 黃幹曰：「道之正統待人而後傳，自周以來，任傳道之責者不過數人，而能使斯道章章較著者，一二人而止耳。

translations.literal: Huang Gan said: "The orthodox transmission of the Way depends on the right person before it can be passed on. Since the Zhou, those who bore the responsibility of transmitting the Way have numbered only a few, and those who could make this Way clearly and distinctly manifest have been but one or two.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gan said: "The true line of the Way waits upon the right person before it can be handed down. Since the Zhou, only a handful have shouldered the task of transmitting the Way, and only one or two at most have ever made that Way stand out plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 由孔子而後，曾子、子思繼其微，至孟子而始著。

translations.literal: After Confucius, Zengzi and Zisi continued its subtle thread; only with Mencius did it become fully manifest.
translations.idiomatic: After Confucius, Zengzi and Zisi kept its faint thread alive; not until Mencius did it shine forth in full.

sentences.zh: 由孟子而後，周、程、張子繼其絕，至熹而始著。」

translations.literal: After Mencius, Zhou, the Chengs, and Master Zhang continued its broken line; only with Xi did it become fully manifest again."
translations.idiomatic: After Mencius, Zhou Dunyi, the Chengs, and Zhang Zai took up the broken line; not until Zhu Xi did it shine forth again."

sentences.zh: 識者以為知言。

translations.literal: Those who understood the matter regarded this as true insight.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment judged this well said.

sentences.zh: 熹子在，紹定中為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Xi's son Zai, during the Shaoding period, served as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi's son Zhu Zai served as Vice Minister of Personnel during the Shaoding era.

sentences.zh: 張栻字敬夫，丞相浚子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi, styled Jingfu, was the son of Chief Councilor Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi, styled Jingfu, was the son of Chief Councilor Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 穎悟夙成，浚愛之，自幼學，所教莫非仁義忠孝之實。

translations.literal: Precocious and quick from youth, Jun loved him; from childhood in his studies, everything he was taught was the substance of humaneness, righteousness, loyalty, and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and mature beyond his years, Zhang Jun doted on him; from boyhood every lesson he received was grounded in humaneness, righteousness, loyalty, and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 長師胡宏，宏一見，即以孔門論仁親切之旨告之。

translations.literal: When grown he took Hu Hong as teacher; at their first meeting Hu Hong immediately told him the intimate purpose of the Confucian school's discourse on humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied under Hu Hong, who at their very first meeting expounded to him the inner meaning of the sage school's teaching on humaneness.

sentences.zh: 栻退而思，若有得焉，宏稱之曰：「聖門有人矣。」

translations.literal: Shi withdrew to reflect and seemed to have gained something; Hong praised him, saying: "The sage's school has found its man."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi withdrew to ponder and seemed to have grasped something; Hu Hong exclaimed, "The sage's gate has its man."

sentences.zh: 栻益自奮厲，以古聖賢自期，作《希顏錄》。

translations.literal: Shi redoubled his striving, setting his expectations against the ancient sages, and wrote Records of Aspiring to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi drove himself harder still, measuring himself against the ancient sages, and composed the Records of Aspiring to Yan.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補官，辟宣撫司都督府書寫機宜文字，除直密閣，時孝宗新即位，浚起謫籍，開府治戎，參佐皆極一時之選。

translations.literal: He entered office through hereditary privilege, was appointed clerk for strategic documents in the military governor's headquarters of the Pacification Commission, and was made Direct Associate of the Secret Palace Library. At that time Emperor Xiaozong had just acceded; Jun was recalled from exile, established a headquarters to manage military affairs, and his staff were all the finest choices of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He received office by inherited privilege, was appointed clerk for confidential military documents in the Pacification Commission headquarters, and was made Direct Associate of the Secret Palace Library. Xiaozong had just taken the throne; Zhang Jun was recalled from banishment, opened a command headquarters, and gathered a staff drawn from the best men of the day.

sentences.zh: 栻時以少年，內贊密謀，外參庶務，其所綜畫，幕府諸人皆自以為不及也。

translations.literal: Shi, though still a youth, advised on secret plans within and participated in general affairs without; in his comprehensive designs, everyone in the staff felt themselves surpassed.
translations.idiomatic: Though still very young, Zhang Shi helped shape secret strategy within and handled public business without; in the plans he drew up, every man in the staff felt himself outmatched.

sentences.zh: 間以軍事入奏，因進言曰：「陛下上念宗社之仇恥，下閔中原之塗炭，惕然於中，而思有以振之。

translations.literal: Occasionally he entered the capital to report on military matters and took the opportunity to say: "Your Majesty, thinking above of the shame owed to the altars of state and below grieving the charred ruin of the Central Plain, is inwardly vigilant and seeks some means to revive it.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he came to court to report on military affairs and seized the moment to say: "Your Majesty, mindful above of the shame our altars of state still bear and grieving below the scorched desolation of the Central Plain, feels this urgency within and seeks some way to rouse the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣謂此心之發，即天理之所存也。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the stirring of this heart is precisely where Heavenly principle resides.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes that the awakening of this heart is itself the presence of Heavenly principle.

sentences.zh: 願益加省察，而稽古親賢以自輔，無使其或少息，則今日之功可以必成，而因循之弊可革矣。」

translations.literal: I wish you would further examine yourself, take antiquity as your measure and draw close to the worthy to aid yourself, and not let this intention slacken even slightly—then today's enterprise can surely succeed and the harm of inertia can be reformed."
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to examine yourself all the more closely, take antiquity as your guide and draw worthy men close to assist you, and never let this resolve slacken even for a moment—then the work of this day can surely be accomplished and the evil of drift and delay can be uprooted."

sentences.zh: 孝宗異其言，於是遂定君臣之契。

translations.literal: Xiaozong was struck by his words, and thus their bond as ruler and minister was firmly established.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was moved by what he heard, and from that moment a true bond was fixed between sovereign and minister.

sentences.zh: 浚去位，湯思退用事，遂罷兵講和。

translations.literal: When Jun left office, Tang Situi wielded power, and military action was halted in favor of peace negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Jun was removed, Tang Situi came to power and the armies were stood down in favor of peace talks.

sentences.zh: 金人乘間縱兵入淮甸，中外大震，廟堂猶主和議，至敕諸將無得輒稱兵。

translations.literal: The Jurchens seized the opportunity to unleash troops into the Huai region; court and country were greatly shaken, yet the court still favored peace talks, even ordering the generals not to take military action on their own.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens seized the moment to send troops flooding into the Huai region; shock ran through court and country, yet the throne still clung to peace and even ordered the generals not to mobilize on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 時浚已沒，栻營葬甫畢，即拜疏言：「吾與金人有不共戴天之仇，異時朝廷雖嘗興縞素之師，然旋遣玉帛之使，是以講和之念未忘於胸中，而至忱惻怛之心無以感格於天人之際，此所以事屢敗而功不成也。

translations.literal: Jun had already died; Shi had just finished arranging his burial when he immediately submitted a memorial saying: "We bear with the Jurchens a hatred that cannot share the same sky. In times past the court may have raised armies in white mourning, yet soon sent envoys bearing jade and silk—thus the thought of peace negotiations has never been forgotten in the breast, and the most sincere, compassionate heart cannot move Heaven and human affairs to respond—this is why undertakings repeatedly fail and achievements are not accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was already dead; Zhang Shi had barely finished his funeral when he submitted a memorial: "We share with the Jurchens a hatred that cannot live under the same sky. In the past the court has sometimes raised armies in mourning white, yet just as quickly dispatched envoys laden with tribute—so the thought of peace has never left the breast, and the deepest sincerity cannot move Heaven and men to answer. That is why efforts fail again and again and nothing is ever achieved.

sentences.zh: 今雖重為群邪所誤，以蹙國而召寇，然亦安知非天欲以是開聖心哉。

translations.literal: Now, though we have again been gravely misled by a crowd of wicked men, contracting the state and inviting invaders, who knows but that Heaven does not wish by this very means to awaken the sacred heart?
