translations.idiomatic: Now, though wicked men have once more led us astray, shrinking the realm and inviting invasion, who is to say Heaven does not mean by this very crisis to open the sacred heart?

sentences.zh: 謂宜深察此理，使吾胸中了然無纖芥之惑，然後明詔中外，公行賞罰，以快軍民之憤，則人心悅，士氣充，而敵不難卻矣。

translations.literal: I say you should deeply examine this principle, until in your breast there is not the slightest mote of confusion; then proclaim it clearly within and without the court, openly dispense rewards and punishments to satisfy the anger of soldiers and civilians—then hearts will rejoice, martial spirit will be full, and the enemy will not be hard to repulse.
translations.idiomatic: You should ponder this deeply until not a trace of doubt remains in your breast; then proclaim it plainly throughout the realm, reward and punish openly to satisfy the rage of soldiers and people—and hearts will rally, morale will rise, and the enemy will not be hard to drive back.

sentences.zh: 繼今以往，益堅此志，誓不言和，專務自強，雖折不撓，使此心純一，貫徹上下，則遲以歲月，亦何功之不濟哉？」

translations.literal: From this day forward, strengthen this resolve yet further: swear never to speak of peace, devote yourself solely to self-strengthening, and though broken, do not bend—let this heart be pure and single, penetrating from above to below; then given time, what achievement could fail to come?"
translations.idiomatic: From this day on, hold this resolve all the firmer: swear never to speak of peace, devote yourself wholly to strengthening the state, and though broken do not bend—let this heart be pure and undivided, reaching from the throne to the ranks below; given time, what goal could fail?"

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted; there was no response.

sentences.zh: 久之，劉珙薦於上，除知撫州，未上，改嚴州。

translations.literal: After some time Liu Gong recommended him to the throne; he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou, but before taking up the post was transferred to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Liu Gong recommended him to the throne; he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou, but before he could take up the post was reassigned to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時宰相虞允文以恢復自任，然所以求者類非其道，意栻素論當與己合，數遣人致殷勤，栻不答。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Councilor Yu Yunwen took recovery of the lost territory as his personal charge, yet the means by which he pursued it were mostly not the right path; he thought Shi's longstanding views ought to agree with his own and repeatedly sent people with cordial messages; Shi did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Yu Yunwen had taken the recovery of lost territory as his personal mission, yet the methods he pursued were largely wrong; assuming Zhang Shi's long-held views would align with his own, he sent envoys again and again with warm overtures—and Zhang Shi never replied.

sentences.zh: 入奏，首言：「先王所以建事立功無不如志者，以其胸中之誠有以感格天人之心，而與之無間也。

translations.literal: On entering the capital to report, he spoke first: "The reason the former kings accomplished undertakings and established achievements without fail was that the sincerity in their breasts could move Heaven and human hearts to respond, without any gap between them.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court to report, he began: "The reason the ancient kings succeeded in every enterprise they undertook was that the sincerity in their hearts could move Heaven and men to respond, with no breach between them.

sentences.zh: 今規畫雖勞，而事功不立，陛下誠深察之日用之間，念慮雲為之際，亦有私意之發以害吾之誠者乎？

translations.literal: Now plans are painstaking yet achievements are not established—does Your Majesty truly examine deeply, in the affairs of daily use and at the moment of thought and action, whether private intentions arise to harm our sincerity?
translations.idiomatic: Plans are drawn up with great labor yet nothing is accomplished—does Your Majesty truly look deep into the daily round of affairs, into every moment of thought and deed, to see whether private motives creep in to corrupt our sincerity?

sentences.zh: 有則克而去之，使吾中局洞然無所間雜，則見義必精，守義必固，而天人之應將不待求而得矣。

translations.literal: If there are, conquer and remove them, so that our inner core is clear and nothing intrusive remains—then seeing righteousness will surely be precise, holding to righteousness will surely be firm, and Heaven and human response will be obtained without having to seek them.
translations.idiomatic: If there are, root them out, until the inner mind is clear and nothing alien remains—then to see righteousness will be to see it truly, to hold righteousness will be to hold it fast, and Heaven and men will answer without your having to ask.

sentences.zh: 夫欲復中原之地，先有以得中原之心，欲得中原之心，先有以得吾民之心。

translations.literal: To wish to recover the lands of the Central Plain, one must first win the hearts of the Central Plain; to win the hearts of the Central Plain, one must first win the hearts of our own people.
translations.idiomatic: To recover the Central Plain you must first win the hearts of the Central Plain; to win the hearts of the Central Plain you must first win the hearts of your own people.

sentences.zh: 求所以得吾民之心者，豈有他哉？

translations.literal: To seek the means of winning our people's hearts—is there anything else?
translations.idiomatic: And how do you win your people's hearts? Is there any other way?

sentences.zh: 不盡其力，不傷其財而已矣。

translations.literal: Only: do not exhaust their strength, do not harm their wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Only this: do not exhaust their strength, do not drain their wealth.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，固當以明大義、正人心為本。

translations.literal: Today's affairs should firmly take clarifying the great righteousness and rectifying people's hearts as the root.
translations.idiomatic: Today's task must take as its foundation the clarification of great principle and the rectification of the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 然其所施有先後，則其緩急不可以不詳；

translations.literal: Yet in what is applied there is order of priority—urgency and delay must be carefully weighed;
translations.idiomatic: Yet what is to be done has its proper sequence, and what is urgent and what can wait must be weighed with care;

sentences.zh: 所務有名實，則其取捨不可以不審，此又明主所宜深察也。」

translations.literal: what is pursued must have both name and reality—choices of what to take and leave must be carefully judged; this too is what an enlightened sovereign ought to examine deeply."
translations.idiomatic: what is undertaken must have both name and substance, and what to adopt and what to set aside must be judged with equal care—this too is what a wise ruler must examine deeply."

sentences.zh: 明年，召為吏部侍郎，兼權起居郎侍立官。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned as Vice Minister of Personnel, concurrently acting Attendant-in-Waiting of the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled as Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrently made acting Attendant-in-Waiting of the Diary of Activity and Repose.

sentences.zh: 時宰方謂敵勢衰弱可圖，建議遣泛使往責陵寢之故，士大夫有憂其無備而召兵者，輒斥去之。

translations.literal: The chief councilor at the time considered the enemy weakened and ripe for exploitation; he proposed sending unrestricted envoys to reproach them over the imperial tombs; literati who feared this lack of preparation would invite war were promptly dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor then believed the enemy enfeebled and ripe for pressure; he proposed sending unrestricted envoys to demand an accounting for the desecration of the imperial tombs, and any scholar-official who warned that such unpreparedness would provoke war was promptly silenced.

sentences.zh: 栻見上，上曰：「卿知敵國事乎？」

translations.literal: When Shi had audience with the Emperor, the Emperor said: "Do you know affairs of the enemy state?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shi had audience, the emperor asked: "Do you know what is happening in the enemy state?"

sentences.zh: 栻對曰：「不知也。」

translations.literal: Shi replied: "I do not."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi answered: "I do not."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「金國饑饉連年，盜賊四起。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Jin state has suffered famine year after year; bandits have risen everywhere."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Jin have suffered famine year after year, and bandits have risen on every side."

sentences.zh: 栻曰：「金人之事，臣雖不知，境中之事，則知之矣。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "As for Jin affairs, though your subject does not know them, affairs within our borders—I do know those."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi said: "I may not know what is happening among the Jin, but I do know what is happening within our own borders."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何也？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "How so?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "How so?"

sentences.zh: 栻曰：「臣切見比年諸道多水旱，民貧日甚，而國家兵弱財匱，官吏誕謾，不足倚賴。

translations.literal: Shi said: "Your subject has closely observed that in recent years many circuits have suffered flood and drought; the people grow poorer daily, while the state is militarily weak and financially depleted, and officials are deceitful—not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi said: "I have seen with my own eyes that in recent years flood and drought have struck many circuits, the people grow poorer by the day, the state is weak in arms and empty in coffers, and officials are feckless and unreliable.

sentences.zh: 正使彼實可圖，臣懼我之未足以圖彼也。」

translations.literal: Even if they truly could be exploited, your subject fears we are not yet adequate to exploit them."
translations.idiomatic: Even if they truly are vulnerable, I fear we are not yet strong enough to take advantage of them."

sentences.zh: 上為默然久之。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent for a long time.

sentences.zh: 栻因出所奏疏讀之曰：「臣竊謂陵寢隔絕，誠臣子不忍言之至痛，然今未能奉辭以討之，又不能正名以絕之，乃欲卑祠厚禮以求於彼，則于大義已為未盡。

translations.literal: Shi then produced and read aloud from his submitted memorial: "Your subject humbly holds that separation from the imperial tombs is indeed the utmost pain that ministers and sons cannot bear to speak of—yet now, unable to rightfully proclaim and punish, and unable to correct the names and cut ties, you wish to send humble petitions and lavish gifts to seek from them—in great righteousness this is already incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi then took out his memorial and read from it: "The severance from our imperial tombs is, I know, a grief ministers and sons can scarcely bear to utter—yet now, unable to send a righteous proclamation to punish them, unable even to declare the rupture by name, you would send humble petitions and lavish gifts to beg from them—in the matter of great principle this is already a compromise too far.

sentences.zh: 而異論者猶以為憂，則其淺陋畏怯，固益甚矣。

translations.literal: Yet those of dissenting views still call this worrisome—then their shallowness and timidity are indeed all the greater.
translations.idiomatic: And if dissenters still call this reckless, then their timidity and smallness of vision are all the more plain.

sentences.zh: 然臣竊揆其心意，或者亦有以見我未有必勝之形，而不能不憂也歟。

translations.literal: Yet your subject ventures to infer their intention: perhaps they also see that we lack the form of certain victory and must worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I suspect their real fear is that they see we do not yet have the look of certain victory—and cannot help worrying.

sentences.zh: 蓋必勝之形，當在於早正素定之時，而不在於兩陣決機之日。」

translations.literal: For the form of certain victory ought to lie in the time of early rectification and settled resolve—not on the day when the two armies decide the outcome."
translations.idiomatic: The look of certain victory is won in the time of early resolve and settled principle—not on the day the two armies meet in the field."

sentences.zh: 上為竦聽改容。

translations.literal: The Emperor listened with startled attention and changed expression.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor listened with rapt attention, his face altered.

sentences.zh: 栻復讀曰：「今日但當下哀痛之詔，明復仇之義，顯絕金人，不與通使。

translations.literal: Shi read on: "Today we need only issue a proclamation of grief, clarify the righteousness of vengeance, openly break with the Jurchens, and send no envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi read on: "Today you need only issue a proclamation of grief, proclaim the duty of vengeance, openly sever relations with the Jurchens, and send no envoys.

sentences.zh: 然後修德立政，用賢養民，選將帥，練甲兵，通內修外攘、進戰退守以為一事，且必治其實而不為虛文，則必勝之形隱然可見，雖有淺陋畏怯之人，亦且奮躍而爭先矣。」

translations.literal: Then cultivate virtue and establish good governance, employ the worthy and nurture the people, select generals, drill armor and troops—unite internal cultivation and external defense, advance and retreat as one enterprise—and must address the substance, not empty formulae; then the form of certain victory will subtly become visible, and even shallow, timid men will leap forward to take the lead."
translations.idiomatic: Then cultivate virtue and good governance, employ worthy men and nurture the people, choose generals, drill the armies—make internal reform and external defense one single task, and see to substance, not empty show—and the look of certain victory will quietly take shape; even the timid and small-minded will leap forward to lead the charge."

sentences.zh: 上為歎息褒諭，以為前始未聞此論也。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed in admiration and praised him, saying he had never heard such a view before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration and praised him, saying he had never heard such an argument before.

sentences.zh: 其後因賜對反復前說，上益嘉歎，面諭：「當以卿為講官，冀時得晤語也。」

translations.literal: Thereafter in granted audiences he repeated these points; the Emperor praised him yet more and personally instructed: "You shall be made a lecturer, so that I may speak with you from time to time."
translations.idiomatic: In later audiences he returned to the same theme again and again; the emperor praised him all the more and told him face to face: "I shall appoint you lecturer, so that we may speak together from time to time."

sentences.zh: 會史正志為發運使，名為均輸，實盡奪州縣財賦，遠近騷然，士大夫爭言其害，栻亦以為言。

translations.literal: When Shi Zhengzhi became transport commissioner, calling his policy "balanced transport" but in reality stripping prefectures and counties of all fiscal resources, disturbance spread near and far; literati competed to speak of its harm, and Shi spoke on it as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Zhengzhi became transport commissioner, his policy—called "balanced transport"—in fact stripped prefectures and counties of all their revenue; unrest spread far and wide, scholars competed to denounce it, and Zhang Shi spoke against it as well.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「正志謂但取之諸郡，非取之於民也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Zhengzhi says he takes only from the various prefectures, not from the people."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Zhengzhi says he takes only from the prefectures, not from the people."

sentences.zh: 栻曰：「今日州郡財賦大抵無餘，若取之不已，而經用有闕，不過巧為名色以取之於民耳。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "Today prefectures and counties generally have no surplus; if taking continues without end and routine expenses fall short, it will be nothing but inventing labels to take from the people."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi said: "Prefectures and counties today have scarcely anything left; if the taking never stops and ordinary expenses fall short, they will simply invent new levies and take from the people in the end."

sentences.zh: 上矍然曰：「如卿之言，是朕假手於發運使以病吾民也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor started and said: "As you say, I would be using the transport commissioner as my hand to afflict my people."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started in alarm: "If what you say is true, then I am using the transport commissioner as my instrument to harm my own people."

sentences.zh: 旋閱其實，果如栻言，即詔罷之。

translations.literal: He soon examined the facts and found it exactly as Shi had said; an edict immediately abolished the policy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon looked into the matter and found it exactly as Zhang Shi had said; an edict immediately abolished the policy.

sentences.zh: 兼侍講，除左司員外郎。

translations.literal: He was concurrently made Lecturer-in-Waiting and appointed Vice Director in the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently made Lecturer-in-Waiting and appointed Vice Director in the Left Bureau.

sentences.zh: 講《詩葛覃》，進說：「治生於敬畏，亂起於驕淫。

translations.literal: Lecturing on the Book of Poetry, "Ge Tan," he advanced the teaching: "Order arises from reverent awe; disorder begins from arrogance and excess.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturing on the "Ge Tan" ode in the Book of Poetry, he taught: "Good order is born of reverent awe; disorder springs from pride and excess.

sentences.zh: 使為國者每念稼穡之勞，而其后妃不忘織絍之事，則心不存者寡矣。」

translations.literal: If those who govern the state always remember the labor of sowing and reaping, and their consorts never forget the work of spinning hemp thread—then those without such a heart would be few."
translations.idiomatic: If rulers always kept in mind the toil of sowing and reaping, and their consorts never forgot the labor of spinning and weaving, few hearts would remain untouched by such feeling."

sentences.zh: 因上陳祖宗自家刑國之懿，下斥今日興利擾民之害。

translations.literal: He then set forth above the fine model of the founders governing the family and punishing the realm, and below condemned the harm of today's profit-seeking that harasses the people.
translations.idiomatic: Above he held up the founders' noble example of governing family and state by moral example; below he condemned the harm of today's profit-seeking that harasses the people.

sentences.zh: 上歎曰：「此王安石所謂'人言不足恤'者，所以為誤國也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed: "This is what Wang Anshi meant by 'the talk of men is not worth heeding'—that is how he brought the state to ruin."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed: "This is what Wang Anshi meant by 'public opinion is not worth worrying about'—and that is how he ruined the state."

sentences.zh: 知閣門事張說除簽書樞密院事，栻夜草疏極諫其不可，旦詣朝堂，質責宰相虞允文曰：「宦官執政，自京、黼始，近習執政，自相公始。」

translations.literal: When Zhang Shuo, Director of the Bureau of Reception, was appointed Assistant Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Shi drafted a memorial overnight strongly remonstrating against it, and at dawn went to the court hall to confront Chief Councilor Yu Yunwen directly: "Eunuchs holding power began with Jing and Fu; favorites holding power begins with you, Lord Chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shuo, Director of the Bureau of Reception, was appointed Assistant Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Zhang Shi drafted a memorial overnight fiercely opposing the appointment and at dawn went to the court hall to confront Chief Councilor Yu Yunwen: "Eunuchs in power began with Jing and Fu; favorites in power begins with you, Lord Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 允文慚憤不堪。

translations.literal: Yunwen was shamed and furious beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen was shamed and enraged beyond endurance.

sentences.zh: 栻復奏：「文武誠不可偏，然今欲右武以均二柄，而所用乃得如此之人，非惟不足以服文吏之心，正恐反激武臣之怒。」

translations.literal: Shi submitted again: "Civil and military truly cannot be one-sided—but now, wishing to elevate military affairs to balance the two handles, the person chosen is such as this; not only will this fail to win the hearts of civil officials—it may well provoke the anger of military officers."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi memorialized again: "Civil and military power must indeed be balanced—but to elevate military affairs and then appoint a man like this will not only fail to win over civil officials; it may well enrage the military officers themselves."

sentences.zh: 孝宗感悟，命得中寢。

translations.literal: Xiaozong understood and ordered the appointment suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong took his point and ordered the appointment withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 然宰相實陰附說，明年出栻知袁州，申說前命，中外喧嘩，說竟以謫死。

translations.literal: Yet the chief councilor secretly favored Shuo; the next year he sent Shi out as prefect of Yuanzhou and reinstated Shuo's previous appointment; court and country erupted in uproar, and Shuo ultimately died in demotion.
translations.idiomatic: But the chief councilor secretly backed Zhang Shuo; the next year he sent Zhang Shi out as prefect of Yuanzhou and reinstated Shuo's appointment; uproar shook court and country, and Shuo ultimately died in exile.

sentences.zh: 栻在朝未期歲，而召對至六七，所言大抵皆修身務學，畏天恤民，抑僥倖，屏讒諛，於是宰相益憚之，而近習尤不悅。

translations.literal: Shi had not yet been a full year at court when he was summoned to audience six or seven times; what he spoke of was largely self-cultivation and diligent study, reverence for Heaven and pity for the people, restraining opportunism, and barring sycophants—so the chief councilor feared him all the more, and the favorites were especially displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi had not yet served a full year at court when he was summoned to audience six or seven times; his themes were self-cultivation and earnest study, reverence for Heaven and compassion for the people, curbing opportunism and shutting out flatterers—so the chief councilor feared him all the more, and the emperor's favorites were especially displeased.

sentences.zh: 退而家居累年，孝宗念之，詔除舊職，知靜江府，經略安撫廣南西路。

translations.literal: He withdrew and lived at home for several years; Xiaozong remembered him, issued an edict restoring his former rank, and appointed him prefect of Jingjiang Prefecture and military commissioner and pacification commissioner of the Guangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and lived in retirement for several years; Xiaozong remembered him, restored his former rank by edict, and appointed him prefect of Jingjiang and military commissioner and pacification commissioner of the Guangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 所部荒殘多盜，栻至，簡州兵，汰冗補闕，籍諸州黥卒伉健者為效用，日習月按，申嚴保伍法。

translations.literal: His jurisdiction was desolate and ravaged, with many bandits; when Shi arrived he streamlined state troops, cut redundancy and filled gaps, registered strong tattooed convicts from various prefectures as militia effectiveness troops, drilled them daily and inspected monthly, and strictly enforced the mutual-responsibility militia system.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction was wasted and lawless, with bandits everywhere; on arrival Zhang Shi trimmed the prefectural forces, cut dead weight and filled gaps, enrolled the sturdiest tattooed convicts from the prefectures as militia, drilled them daily and inspected them monthly, and strictly enforced the mutual-responsibility militia system.

sentences.zh: 諭溪峒酋豪弭怨睦鄰，毋相殺掠，於是群蠻帖服。

translations.literal: He instructed chieftains of stream grottoes to end grievances, live in harmony with neighbors, and refrain from mutual killing and plunder—whereupon the tribal peoples submitted peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the chieftains of the stream grottoes to lay aside old grudges, live in peace with their neighbors, and cease raiding one another—and the tribal peoples submitted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷買馬橫山，歲久弊滋，邊氓告病，而馬不時至。

translations.literal: The court had for years been buying horses at Hengshan; over time abuses multiplied, border people complained of hardship, and horses did not arrive on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: For years the court had been buying horses at Hengshan; abuses mounted, border people groaned under the burden, and horses failed to arrive on time.

sentences.zh: 栻究其利病六十餘條，奏革之，諸蠻感悅，爭以善馬至。

translations.literal: Shi investigated more than sixty points of benefit and harm, memorialized reforms, and the various tribes, moved and pleased, competed to bring fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi investigated more than sixty abuses, memorialized reforms, and the tribal peoples, grateful and pleased, competed to bring their best horses.

sentences.zh: 孝宗聞栻治行，詔特進秩，直寶文閣，因任。

translations.literal: Xiaozong heard of Shi's governance and issued an edict specially advancing his rank to Direct Associate of the Hall of Treasured Classics, retaining him in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong heard of Zhang Shi's record in office, he issued an edict specially promoting him to Direct Associate of the Hall of Treasured Classics while keeping him in post.

sentences.zh: 尋除秘閣修撰、荊湖北路轉運副使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Compiler in the Secret Archive and Vice Transport Commissioner of the Jinghu North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Compiler in the Secret Archive and Vice Transport Commissioner of the Jinghu North Circuit.

sentences.zh: 改知江陵府，安撫本路。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Jiangling Prefecture and pacification commissioner of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Jiangling and pacification commissioner of that circuit.

sentences.zh: 一日去貪吏十四人。

translations.literal: In a single day he removed fourteen greedy officials.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day he dismissed fourteen corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 湖北多盜，府縣往往縱釋以病良民，栻首劾大吏之縱賊者，捕斬奸民之舍賊者，令其黨得相捕告以除罪，群盜皆遁去。

translations.literal: Hubei had many bandits; prefectures and counties often released them to harm lawful people; Shi first impeached high officials who released bandits, captured and executed wicked men who harbored bandits, ordered their associates to capture one another and report in exchange for remission of guilt—and the bandit gangs all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rife in Hubei; prefectures and counties often released criminals to the harm of honest people; Zhang Shi first impeached senior officials who had let bandits go, seized and executed men who harbored them, offered their accomplices remission if they informed on one another—and the bandit gangs dispersed.

sentences.zh: 郡瀕邊屯，主將與帥守每不相下，栻以禮遇諸將，得其歡心，又加恤士伍，勉以忠義，隊長有功輒補官，士鹹感奮。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered garrison lands; commanders and the military prefect often looked down on each other; Shi treated the generals with courtesy and won their goodwill, further showed care for the ranks, encouraged them with loyalty and righteousness, and whenever squad leaders achieved merit promptly supplemented their offices—the soldiers were all moved and stirred to effort.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lay on the frontier; garrison commanders and the prefect often clashed; Zhang Shi treated the generals with courtesy and won their hearts, showed special care for the rank and file, urged them on with talk of loyalty and duty, and promptly rewarded squad leaders who distinguished themselves with official rank—and the soldiers were stirred to serve with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 並淮奸民出塞為盜者，捕得數人，有北方亡奴亦在盜中。

translations.literal: Wicked men along the Huai who crossed the border to rob were captured, several in number; among the bandits was also a fugitive slave from the north.
translations.idiomatic: Several ruffians from along the Huai who had crossed the border to plunder were captured; among them was a fugitive slave from the north.

sentences.zh: 栻曰：「朝廷未能正名討敵，無使疆場之事其曲在我。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "The court has not yet corrected names to punish the enemy—let us not let frontier affairs show us in the wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi said: "The court has not yet formally declared war on the enemy—we must not let a frontier incident put us in the wrong."

sentences.zh: 命斬之以徇於境，而縛其亡奴歸之。

translations.literal: He ordered the bandits executed and displayed at the border as a warning, and bound the fugitive slave to return him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the bandits executed and their bodies displayed at the border as a warning, and sent the fugitive slave back in bonds.

sentences.zh: 北人歎曰：「南朝有人。」

translations.literal: Northerners sighed: "The Southern court has its men."
translations.idiomatic: Northerners marveled: "The Southern court has men of principle."

sentences.zh: 信陽守劉大辯怙勢希賞，廣招流民，而奪見戶熟田以與之。

translations.literal: Xinyang prefect Liu Dabian relied on influence to seek rewards, broadly recruited displaced persons, and seized established households' cultivated fields to give to them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dabian, prefect of Xinyang, traded on influence to win favor, recruited displaced persons on a large scale, and seized cultivated land from established households to give to them.

sentences.zh: 栻劾大辨詐諼，所招流民不滿百，而虛增其數十倍，請論其罪，不報。

translations.literal: Shi impeached Dabian for fraud, noting the displaced recruited numbered fewer than a hundred yet were falsely reported tenfold; he requested punishment—no response.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi impeached Dabian for fraud, showing that fewer than a hundred displaced persons had been recruited yet the numbers were inflated tenfold; he asked that Dabian be punished—there was no response.

sentences.zh: 章累上，大辯易他郡，栻自以不得其職求去，詔以右文殿修撰提舉武夷山沖佑觀。

translations.literal: Memorials piled up; Dabian was transferred to another prefecture; Shi, feeling he could not fulfill his duties, requested resignation; an edict made him Compiler in the Hall of Culture and Classics and superintendent of the Chongyou Temple on Mount Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial after memorial went up; Dabian was transferred to another post; Zhang Shi, feeling he could no longer serve effectively, asked to resign; an edict appointed him Compiler in the Hall of Culture and Classics and superintendent of the Chongyou Temple on Mount Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 病且死，猶手疏勸上親君子遠小人，信任防一己之偏，好惡公天下之理。

translations.literal: Nearing death from illness, he still wrote by hand a memorial urging the Emperor to be close to gentlemen and distant from petty men, to guard against partiality in trust, and to make likes and dislikes accord with the principle of the public realm under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: As illness brought him near death, he still wrote a memorial by hand urging the emperor to draw close to gentlemen and keep petty men at a distance, to guard against partiality in whom he trusted, and to let likes and dislikes be governed by what is right for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天下傳誦之。

translations.literal: The realm transmitted and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm copied and recited it.

sentences.zh: 栻有公輔之望，卒時年四十有八。

translations.literal: Shi had been expected to reach the highest ministerial offices; he died at the age of forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi had been widely expected to reach the highest offices; he died at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 孝宗聞之，深為嗟悼，四方賢士大夫往往出涕相吊，而江陵、靜江之民尤哭之哀。

translations.literal: Xiaozong heard and deeply mourned; worthy literati throughout the land often shed tears in mutual lament, and the people of Jiangling and Jingjiang wept most bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong heard the news he mourned deeply; worthy scholars throughout the realm wept in one another's company, and the people of Jiangling and Jingjiang grieved most bitterly of all.

sentences.zh: 嘉定間，賜諡曰宣。

translations.literal: During the Jiading period he was posthumously granted the temple name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiading era he was posthumously granted the temple name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 淳祐初，詔從祀孔子廟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunyou, an edict added him as collateral sacrifice in the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chunyou era, an edict enshrined him as a collateral sacrifice in Confucius's temple.

sentences.zh: 栻為人表裏洞然，勇於從義，無毫髮滯吝。

translations.literal: Shi's person was transparent inside and out; he was bold in following righteousness, without the slightest hesitation or stinting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi was transparent through and through—bold in following righteousness, without a hair's breadth of hesitation or holding back.

sentences.zh: 每進對，必自盟於心，不可以人主意悅輒有所隨順。

translations.literal: Each time he came forward in audience he swore to his own heart that he must not simply go along with whatever pleased the sovereign's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he came before the throne he swore to himself that he would not simply follow whatever happened to please the emperor's mood.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嘗言伏節死義之臣難得，栻對：「當于犯顏敢諫中求之。

translations.literal: Xiaozong once said that ministers who preserve integrity and die for righteousness are hard to find; Shi replied: "One ought to seek them among those who face the sovereign and dare to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong once remarked that ministers who hold fast to principle and die for righteousness are hard to find; Zhang Shi answered: "Look for them among those who face the throne and dare to speak against it.

sentences.zh: 若平時不能犯顏敢諫，他日何望其伏節死義？」

translations.literal: If in ordinary times they cannot face the sovereign and dare to remonstrate, how can one expect them later to preserve integrity and die for righteousness?"
translations.idiomatic: If in ordinary times a man cannot face the throne and speak plainly, how can you expect him later to hold fast and die for principle?"

sentences.zh: 孝宗又言難得辦事之臣，栻對：「陛下當求曉事之臣，不當求辦事之臣。

translations.literal: Xiaozong again spoke of how hard it was to find officials who could get things done; Shi replied: "Your Majesty should seek officials who understand affairs—not officials who merely get things done.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong spoke again of how hard it was to find men who could simply get things done; Zhang Shi replied: "Your Majesty should seek men who understand affairs—not men who merely get things done.

sentences.zh: 若但求辦事之臣，則他日敗陛下事者，未必非此人也。」

translations.literal: If you seek only officials who get things done, then those who someday ruin Your Majesty's affairs may well be precisely these same men."
translations.idiomatic: If you seek only men who get things done, the very men who someday ruin your affairs may well be these same men."

sentences.zh: 栻自言：前後奏對忤上旨雖多，而上每念之，未嘗加怒者，所謂可以理奪雲爾。

translations.literal: Shi himself said: though in audiences before and after he often went against the Emperor's intent, the Emperor always regarded him fondly and never showed anger—what is called being overcome by reason alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi himself said that though in audience after audience he often went against the emperor's wishes, the emperor always thought kindly of him and never showed anger—what is meant by being won over by reason alone.

sentences.zh: 其遠小人尤嚴。

translations.literal: He was especially strict in keeping petty men at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially severe in keeping petty men at a distance.

sentences.zh: 為都司日，肩輿出，遇曾覿，覿舉手欲揖，栻急掩其窗櫺，覿慚，手不得下。

translations.literal: While serving in the capital bureau, he went out in a shoulder-borne sedan and met Zeng Di; Di raised his hand intending to bow; Shi quickly shut his window lattice; Di was ashamed, his hand unable to come down.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the capital, he went out in a sedan chair and met Zeng Di, who raised his hand to bow; Zhang Shi quickly shut his window screen; Di, shamed, could not bring his hand down.

sentences.zh: 所至郡，暇日召諸生告語。

translations.literal: In every prefecture he reached, on free days he summoned students to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: In every prefecture he served, on his free days he gathered students to teach them.

sentences.zh: 民以事至庭，必隨事開曉。

translations.literal: When common people came to court with affairs, he always enlightened them according to the matter at hand.
translations.idiomatic: When common people came to his court with their troubles, he always explained matters to them as the case required.

sentences.zh: 具為條教，大抵以正禮俗、明倫紀為先。

translations.literal: He fully set forth regulations and teachings, putting first rectifying ritual custom and clarifying human bonds and norms.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up full sets of regulations and instruction, putting first the rectification of custom and the clarification of human relationships.

sentences.zh: 斥異端，毀淫祠，而崇社稷山川古先聖賢之祀，舊典所遺，亦以義起也。

translations.literal: He drove out heterodox teachings, destroyed illicit shrines, and honored sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain, mountains and rivers, and ancient sages; where the old canon had omissions, he also established rites according to right principle.
translations.idiomatic: He drove out heterodox teachings, demolished illicit shrines, and restored proper worship of the altars of soil and grain, mountains and rivers, and the ancient sages; where the old rites had lapsed, he re-established them according to right principle.

sentences.zh: 栻聞道甚早，朱熹嘗言：「己之學乃銖積寸累而成，如敬夫，則于大本卓然先有見者也。」

translations.literal: Shi attained the Way very early; Zhu Xi once said: "My own learning was piled up grain by grain and inch by inch; as for Jingfu, he had already attained clear insight into the fundamental root."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi found the Way very early; Zhu Xi once said: "My own learning was built up grain by grain and inch by inch; as for Jingfu, he had already grasped the fundamental root with clear insight."

sentences.zh: 所著《論語孟子說》、《太極圖說》、《洙泗言仁》、《諸葛忠武侯傳》、《經世紀年》，皆行於世。

translations.literal: His works Expositions on the Analects and Mencius, Exposition of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Words on Humaneness at the Zhu and Si, Biography of Zhuge the Loyal Marquis of Wu, and Annals for Governing the Age all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works—the Expositions on the Analects and Mencius, Exposition of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Words on Humaneness at the Zhu and Si, Biography of Zhuge the Loyal Marquis of Wu, and Annals for Governing the Age—all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 栻之言曰：「學莫先於義利之辨。

translations.literal: Shi's saying went: "In learning nothing comes before distinguishing righteousness from profit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi taught: "In learning, nothing comes before distinguishing righteousness from profit.

sentences.zh: 義者，本心之當為，非有為而為也。

translations.literal: Righteousness is what the original heart ought to do—not doing something with ulterior purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness is what the original heart ought to do—not acting from ulterior motive.

sentences.zh: 有為而為，則皆人欲，非天理。」

translations.literal: When one acts with ulterior purpose, all of it is human desire—not Heavenly principle."
translations.idiomatic: When one acts from ulterior motive, all of it is human desire, not Heavenly principle."

sentences.zh: 此栻講學之要也。

translations.literal: This was the essential point of Shi's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: This was the heart of Zhang Shi's teaching.

sentences.zh: 子焯。

translations.literal: His son was Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhang Zhuo.
